rule_text_technical: Each relevant Department of Defense contract entered into after the date the regulations are implemented shall include requirements for the delivery of modular system interfaces, including software-defined interface syntax and properties in machine-readable format, a machine-readable definition of the relationship between the delivered interface and existing common standards, and documentation with functional descriptions of software-defined interfaces conveying semantic meaning.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for defense acquisition must establish repositories documenting AI system interfaces, technical specifications, and implementations, along with a comprehensive index of these materials, within 90 days of policy enactment.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 90 days after enactment, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall direct the Secretaries concerned and heads of appropriate DoD components to establish and maintain repositories for interfaces, syntax and properties, documentation, and communication implementations, establish a comprehensive index thereof, and if practicable establish an alternate reference repository.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You must, as a non-Governmental entity receiving access to interface data from the repositories, not further release, disclose, or use such data except as authorized.
rule_text_technical: A non-Governmental entity that receives access under subparagraph (A) may not further release, disclose, or use such data except as authorized.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for defense must establish and communicate to the legislative body a comprehensive implementation plan with specific timelines for requiring covered entities to register and report beneficial ownership and foreign ownership interests, including designated systems for ongoing disclosure.
rule_text_technical: Not later than March 1, 2021, the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the congressional defense committees a plan and schedule for implementation of the requirements of section 847 of the NDAA for FY2020, including a timeline for issuance of regulations, training, and development of systems for reporting of beneficial ownership and FOCI by covered contractors or subcontractors.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You must include in the Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System database an identification of any beneficial owner of a corporation receiving Federal contract or grant awards.
rule_text_technical: Section 2313(d) of title 41 is amended to require, in the database, an identification of any beneficial owner of any corporation to which a Federal award is made, with definitions of beneficial ownership and corporation provided.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You must, as Secretary, require periodic reports and conduct examinations of covered contractors or subcontractors to assess compliance with FOCI requirements.
rule_text_technical: Section 847(b)(2)(A) of the NDAA for FY2020 is amended to add a requirement for the Secretary to require reports and conduct examinations on a periodic basis of covered contractors or subcontractors in order to assess compliance with the requirements of this section.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The National AI Initiative must terminate 10 years after the date of enactment of the Act.
rule_text_technical: The Initiative established under this division shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Interagency Committee must develop, within 2 years of enactment, a strategic plan for AI (updated at least every 3 years) establishing goals, priorities, and metrics, including support for ethical, legal, safety, security, bias, and societal issues research.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 2 years after enactment, the Interagency Committee shall develop a strategic plan for artificial intelligence (updated at least every 3 years) addressing the elements specified in Sec. 5103(d)(2)(A)-(G).

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Interagency Committee must, beginning FY 2022, submit an annual report to specified congressional committees within 90 days of the President's budget request, summarizing the Initiative's budget and Institutes established.
rule_text_technical: For each fiscal year beginning FY 2022, not later than 90 days after submission of the President's budget request, the Interagency Committee shall submit a report to specified Congressional committees.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Advisory Committee chairperson must establish a Subcommittee on AI and Law Enforcement to advise the President on AI development relating to law enforcement matters.
rule_text_technical: The chairperson of the Advisory Committee shall establish a subcommittee on matters relating to AI development relating to law enforcement, which shall advise the President on the matters listed in Sec. 5104(e)(2).

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Subcommittee shall provide advice on bias and shall require that government and law enforcement use of facial recognition account for ethical considerations and be subject to additional oversight, controls, and limitations as determined by the Subcommittee.
rule_text_technical: The subcommittee shall advise on bias, including whether facial recognition use by government authorities takes into account ethical considerations and whether such use should be subject to additional oversight, controls, and limitations.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Subcommittee must advise on security of data, including law enforcement's access to data and the security parameters for that data.
rule_text_technical: The subcommittee shall provide advice on security of data, including law enforcement's access to data and the security parameters for that data.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Subcommittee must advise on legal standards designed to ensure AI systems are consistent with privacy rights, civil rights, civil liberties, and disability rights.
rule_text_technical: The subcommittee shall advise on legal standards designed to ensure AI systems are consistent with privacy rights, civil rights and civil liberties, and disability rights raised by use of these technologies.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Advisory Committee must submit a report on its findings and recommendations to the President and specified Congressional committees within 1 year of enactment, and at least every 3 years thereafter.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 1 year after enactment, and at least once every 3 years thereafter, the Advisory Committee shall submit a report to the President and specified committees on its findings and recommendations.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies shall commission independent research institutions to conduct a study on the current and future impact of AI on the workforce across sectors, and shall ensure results are made publicly available to inform policy decisions.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 90 days after enactment, the NSF shall enter into a contract with the National Research Council to conduct a study of the current and future impact of artificial intelligence on the US workforce across sectors.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Task Force roadmap must include an assessment of privacy and civil rights and civil liberties requirements associated with the National AI Research Resource and its research.
rule_text_technical: The roadmap shall include an assessment of privacy and civil rights and civil liberties requirements associated with the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource and its research.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Task Force roadmap must include an assessment of security requirements associated with the National AI Research Resource and a recommended framework for management of access controls.
rule_text_technical: The roadmap shall include an assessment of security requirements associated with the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource and recommend a framework for the management of access controls.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Institutes may use funds to develop and manage testbeds for AI systems, including sector-specific testbeds, designed to enable users to evaluate AI systems prior to deployment.
rule_text_technical: Financial assistance may be used for developing and managing testbeds for AI systems, including sector-specific testbeds, designed to enable users to evaluate AI systems prior to deployment.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: No funds authorized in this title may be awarded to Institutes outside the United States; all awardees and subawardees must be based in the United States.
rule_text_technical: No funds authorized in this title shall be awarded to Institutes outside of the United States. All awardees and subawardees for such Institute shall be based in the United States.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: National AI standards bodies shall establish and advance collaborative frameworks, standards, guidelines, and methods for AI development; develop and implement a risk-mitigation framework for deploying AI systems; establish technical standards for trustworthy AI; and establish standards to test for and identify bias in AI training data and applications.
rule_text_technical: The Institute shall advance collaborative frameworks, standards, guidelines, and associated methods and techniques for AI; support development of a risk-mitigation framework for deploying AI; support technical standards for trustworthy AI; and support standards to test for bias in AI training data and applications.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: AI standards bodies may develop and support standards for safety and robustness of AI systems, including assurance, verification, validation, security, control, and the ability to withstand unexpected inputs and adversarial attacks.
rule_text_technical: The Director may support best practices and voluntary standards for safety and robustness of AI systems, including assurance, verification, validation, security, control, and ability to withstand unexpected inputs and adversarial attacks.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

rule_text: AI standards bodies must develop and periodically update a voluntary risk management framework for trustworthy AI systems within a defined timeframe, in collaboration with government science funding agencies and private sector organizations.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 2 years after enactment, the Director shall work to develop, and periodically update, in collaboration with other public and private sector organizations, a voluntary risk management framework for trustworthy AI systems.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The risk management framework must identify and provide standards, guidelines, best practices, methodologies, procedures and processes for developing trustworthy AI systems, assessing trustworthiness, and mitigating risks from AI systems.
rule_text_technical: The framework shall identify and provide standards, guidelines, best practices, methodologies, procedures and processes for developing trustworthy AI systems, assessing trustworthiness of AI systems, and mitigating risks from AI systems.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The risk management framework must establish common definitions and characterizations for aspects of trustworthiness including explainability, transparency, safety, privacy, security, robustness, fairness, bias, ethics, validation, verification, and interpretability.
rule_text_technical: The framework shall establish common definitions and characterizations for aspects of trustworthiness including explainability, transparency, safety, privacy, security, robustness, fairness, bias, ethics, validation, verification, interpretability, and other properties common across all sectors.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The risk management framework must not prescribe or otherwise require the use of specific information or communications technology products or services.
rule_text_technical: The framework shall not prescribe or otherwise require the use of specific information or communications technology products or services.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead environmental science agency must establish a dedicated center or unit for artificial intelligence to coordinate scientific and technological efforts related to AI across the organization and implement a comprehensive program to improve the use of AI systems throughout the agency.
rule_text_technical: The Administrator of NOAA shall establish a Center for Artificial Intelligence to coordinate AI scientific and technological efforts and implement a comprehensive program to improve the use of AI systems across the agency in support of NOAA's mission.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead regulatory authority may withhold AI models or data from disclosure if necessary to protect national security interests, in consultation with the national defense authority as appropriate.
rule_text_technical: Notwithstanding any other provision, the Administrator, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense as appropriate, may withhold models or data used by the Center if necessary to protect national security interests of the United States.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies must, within a defined timeframe following relevant research on AI governance, report to their legislative authority on options for requiring ethics or risk assessments as part of research funding applications for AI or high-risk computing projects.
rule_text_technical: No later than 6 months after publication of the study described in paragraph (1)(C), the Director shall report to Congress on options for requiring an ethics or risk statement as part of all or a subset of applications for research funding to the NSF.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies shall allocate resources to support and fund research and educational initiatives that advance understanding of the ethical, social, safety, and security risks associated with AI systems.
rule_text_technical: The Director shall award grants for AI education research, development, and related activities that increase awareness of potential ethical, social, safety, and security risks of artificial intelligence systems.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies shall provide mandatory support for efforts to achieve equitable access to K-12 artificial intelligence education in diverse geographic areas and for populations historically underrepresented in science, engineering, and artificial intelligence fields.
rule_text_technical: The Director shall award grants supporting efforts to achieve equitable access to K-12 AI education in diverse geographic areas and for populations historically underrepresented in science, engineering, and artificial intelligence fields.

rule_text: The NOAA Administrator may withhold AI models or data used by the Center if necessary to protect U.S. national security interests.
rule_text_technical: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the Administrator, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense as appropriate, may withhold models or data used by the Center if the Administrator determines doing so to be necessary to protect the national security interests of the United States.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies shall allocate resources to support research on trustworthy AI systems, including algorithmic explainability, bias identification and mitigation, and safety and robustness assurance through verification, validation, security, and control measures.
rule_text_technical: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall award financial assistance to eligible entities to carry out research projects on the development of trustworthy artificial intelligence systems, including algorithmic explainability, analytical methods for identifying and mitigating bias in artificial intelligence systems, and safety and robustness, including assurance, verification, validation, security, and control.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Central government oversight bodies must ensure that policies governing AI-related projects include risk management practices aligned with applicable AI risk management frameworks.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary shall review agency policies for risk management in artificial intelligence related projects and issue as necessary policies and principles that are consistent with the framework developed under section 22A(c) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Treasury Secretary must issue a rule specifying standards by which financial institutions test technology and related internal processes designed to facilitate Bank Secrecy Act compliance.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the head of each agency to which the Secretary has delegated duties or powers under subsection (a), shall issue a rule to specify with respect to technology and related technology internal processes designed to facilitate compliance with the requirements under this subchapter, the standards by which financial institutions are to test the technology and related technology internal processes.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Standards for testing financial institution AI/ML compliance technology may include emphasis on innovative approaches like machine learning, risk-based testing pre- and post-implementation, and a risk governance framework for oversight.
rule_text_technical: The standards described in paragraph (1) may include an emphasis on using innovative approaches such as machine learning or other enhanced data analytics processes; risk-based testing, oversight, and other risk management approaches prior to and after implementation; specific criteria for when and how risk-based testing should be considered; and specific standards for a risk governance framework for financial institutions to provide oversight and to prudently evaluate and monitor systems and testing processes both pre- and post-implementation.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Testing standards for financial institution compliance technology must include requirements for appropriate data privacy and information security.
rule_text_technical: The standards described in paragraph (1) may include requirements for appropriate data privacy and information security.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Testing standards must require that system configurations, including any applicable algorithms and validations, used by the compliance regime be disclosed to FinCEN and the appropriate Federal functional regulator upon request.
rule_text_technical: The standards may include a requirement that the system configurations, including any applicable algorithms and any validation of those configurations used by the regime be disclosed to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and the appropriate Federal functional regulator upon request.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Algorithms voluntarily or compulsorily disclosed by financial institutions to a government agency, and any associated creation/adaptation materials, must be treated as confidential and are exempt from FOIA disclosure.
rule_text_technical: If a financial institution or any director, officer, employee, or agent of any financial institution, voluntarily or pursuant to this subsection or any other authority, discloses the algorithms of the financial institution to a government agency, the algorithms and any materials associated with the creation or adaption of such algorithms shall be considered confidential and not subject to public disclosure. Section 552(a)(3) of title 5 (FOIA) shall not apply to any request for such algorithms or associated materials.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Treasury Secretary must analyze the impact of financial technology on financial crimes compliance, including AI-related implications for money laundering, terrorism financing, and other illicit finance.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary, in consultation with financial regulators, technology experts, national security experts, law enforcement, and any other group the Secretary determines is appropriate, shall analyze the impact of financial technology on financial crimes compliance, including with respect to money laundering, the financing of terrorism, proliferation finance, serious tax fraud, trafficking, sanctions evasion, and other illicit finance.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The FinCEN Director must brief Congress within 90 days on the use of emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, digital identity, and distributed ledger technologies, and how AI could improve FinCEN's data analysis.
rule_text_technical: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of FinCEN shall brief the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives on the use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital identity technologies, distributed ledger technologies, and other innovative technologies within FinCEN, and whether such technologies can be further leveraged to make data analysis by FinCEN more efficient and effective.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Rules permitting financial institutions to share suspicious activity report information with foreign branches, subsidiaries, and affiliates must ensure such sharing is subject to appropriate standards regarding data security and confidentiality of personally identifiable information.
rule_text_technical: In issuing the rules required under clause (i), the Secretary shall ensure that the sharing of information described in subparagraph (B) is subject to appropriate standards and requirements regarding data security and the confidentiality of personally identifiable information.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Treasury de-risking review must consider the appropriate manner in which to ensure the security and confidentiality of personal information.
rule_text_technical: The review required under paragraph (2) shall consider the appropriate manner in which to ensure the security and confidentiality of personal information.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Treasury review of currency transaction and suspicious activity reporting requirements must consider the appropriate manner in which to ensure the security and confidentiality of personal information.
rule_text_technical: The review required under subsection (a) shall include a review of the appropriate manner in which to ensure the security and confidentiality of personal information.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You must understand that 'digital content forgery technology' means use of emerging technologies, including AI and machine learning, to fabricate or manipulate audio, visual, or text content with intent to mislead.
rule_text_technical: For purposes of Section 9004, the term 'digital content forgery technology' is defined as the use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques, to fabricate or manipulate audio, visual, or text content with the intent to mislead.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for telecommunications must establish criteria for public grants supporting deployment of open and interoperable wireless technologies, including security features for multi-vendor networks.
rule_text_technical: Under Section 9202(a)(1)(C), the Secretary acting through the NTIA Administrator shall establish grant criteria to support promotion and deployment of technologies enhancing competitiveness in 5G and successor wireless supply chains using open and interoperable interface radio access networks, including security features and network function virtualization.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The NTIA Administrator must identify a process to establish goals for modernizing federal spectrum management infrastructure, including innovative technologies such as cloud-based databases, AI, automation, and improved modeling and simulation capabilities.
rule_text_technical: Per Section 9203(a), the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information shall identify a process to establish goals for modernization of covered agencies' infrastructure for managing Federal spectrum, including standardization of data inputs, modeling algorithms, and innovative capabilities including cloud-based databases, artificial intelligence technologies, automation, and improved modeling and simulation.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The NTIA must ensure its modernized spectrum infrastructure enhances security and reliability so that the agency complies with federal information security requirements under chapter 35 of title 44.
rule_text_technical: Section 9203(b)(2)(D)(i) requires that the NTIA modernization plan detail how the modernized infrastructure will enhance security and reliability so that the NTIA is in compliance with the requirements of subchapter II of chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code (FISMA).

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The Internet of Things working group must examine additional security measures federal agencies need to safely use IoT, including measures ensuring critical infrastructure security and resilience against cyber threats.
rule_text_technical: Under Section 9204(b)(2)(D)(iv), the working group shall examine any additional security measures Federal agencies may need to take to safely and securely use the Internet of Things, including measures that ensure security of critical infrastructure and enhance resiliency of Federal systems against cyber threats to the IoT.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The IoT steering committee must advise on policies, programs, or multi-stakeholder activities promoting the privacy of individuals who use or are affected by the Internet of Things.
rule_text_technical: Pursuant to Section 9204(b)(5)(B)(iv), the steering committee shall advise the working group on policies, programs, or multi-stakeholder activities that promote or are related to the privacy of individuals who use or are affected by the Internet of Things, that may enhance IoT security including critical infrastructure, and that protect users of the IoT.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The IoT working group must submit a report to Congress within 18 months including findings and recommendations on IoT regulation, the steering committee's report, and federal agency progress implementing recommendations.
rule_text_technical: Section 9204(b)(6) requires the working group to submit to Congress, not later than 18 months after enactment, a report including findings and recommendations on IoT-related duties, the steering committee report, recommendations for action or reasons for inaction, and an accounting of progress by Federal agencies in implementing recommendations.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for cybersecurity must develop and submit a national implementation strategy to the relevant legislative body within the specified timeframe to adopt domain-based message authentication standards across all email providers operating within the jurisdiction.
rule_text_technical: Under Section 9006, the Secretary of Homeland Security shall develop and submit a strategy to Congress to implement Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance standards across all U.S.-based email providers at scale, including minimum-size thresholds, security and privacy benefits, stakeholder identification, barriers, and cost estimates.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for veteran services must provide veterans with read-only access to their personal records in printable format through a publicly accessible digital portal.
rule_text_technical: Section 9105 requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide a veteran read-only access to the documents of the veteran contained in the Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record in a printable format through a portal accessible through an internet website of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead regulatory authority responsible for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure must be appointed from individuals with extensive knowledge in at least two of the following areas: cybersecurity, infrastructure security, or security risk management, with a minimum of five years of demonstrated experience in these fields.
rule_text_technical: Section 9001 amends Section 2202(b) of the Homeland Security Act to require that the CISA Director be appointed from individuals with extensive knowledge in at least two specified areas (cybersecurity, infrastructure security, security risk management) and not fewer than five years of demonstrated experience fostering coordination on cybersecurity, infrastructure security, or security risk management.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Each sector-specific regulator must coordinate with relevant defense and security agencies to facilitate sharing of information regarding physical security and cybersecurity threats within its designated critical infrastructure sector, including via information sharing and analysis organizations.
rule_text_technical: New Section 2215(c)(4) of the Homeland Security Act requires Sector Risk Management Agencies to facilitate, in coordination with the CISA Director, the sharing of information with the Department and other Federal departments regarding physical security and cybersecurity threats within the designated sector, including through information sharing and analysis organizations and the national cybersecurity and communications integration center.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund grants must support deployment of security features that enhance the integrity and availability of equipment in multi-vendor wireless networks.
rule_text_technical: Section 9202(a)(1)(C)(vi) directs that Innovation Fund grant criteria support promoting and deploying security features enhancing the integrity and availability of equipment in multi-vendor networks.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Sector-specific regulators responsible for emergency alert systems must establish a system to receive reports of false alerts for the purpose of recording and examining causes of such false alerts.
rule_text_technical: Section 9201(c) requires the Commission, in consultation with the FEMA Administrator, to complete a rulemaking proceeding to establish a system to receive from the Administrator or State, Tribal, or local governments reports of false alerts under the Emergency Alert System or the Wireless Emergency Alerts System for the purpose of recording and examining the causes of such false alerts.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead regulatory authority responsible for social media threat analysis must submit a report to the legislative branch at least 90 days before each general election analyzing foreign malign influence campaigns on social media targeting that election, including bot networks, algorithmic amplification, and machine-manipulated media.
rule_text_technical: The Director of the Center shall, not later than 90 days before each regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report analyzing patterns and techniques of foreign malign influence campaigns on social media platforms by covered foreign countries, including inauthentic accounts and 'bot' networks, the estimated reach and impact of weaponized disinformation including amplification by users and algorithmic distribution, and trends in machine-manipulated media.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for commerce must establish a national cybersecurity challenge to advance cybersecurity efforts in response to emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, quantum science, autonomy, and data science, with a goal of achieving high-priority breakthroughs by 2028.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary of Commerce shall establish a national cybersecurity challenge focused on advancing cybersecurity efforts in response to emerging technology, such as artificial intelligence, quantum science, next generation communications, autonomy, data science, and computational technologies, to achieve high-priority breakthroughs in cybersecurity by 2028.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020
first_instance.citation: Sec. 9407 (new Sec. 205(a)(1)(C) of Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2014)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for commerce and trade must establish a national competition or challenge program focused on advancing digital identity solutions that improve privacy, security, and safety of online activity for individuals while maintaining practical usability.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary of Commerce shall establish a national cybersecurity challenge to maintain a high sense of usability while improving the privacy, security, and safety of online activity of individuals in the United States.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Government science funding agencies must include in their strategic technology reports a plan to significantly increase baseline civilian research and development investments in artificial intelligence and quantum information science over a defined medium-term period.
rule_text_technical: The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy shall include in the report submitted to Congress a plan to double the baseline of civilian research and development investments of the Federal Government in artificial intelligence and quantum information science by fiscal year 2022.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: National AI standards bodies must commission a study and recommendations on the influence of foreign government policies on international standards-setting for emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and quantum information science.
rule_text_technical: The Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology shall enter into an agreement with an appropriate entity to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding how the People's Republic of China is likely to engage in international standardization activities of critical technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum information science, and recommendations on how the United States can mitigate that influence.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You (President) must include in the Continuity of the Economy Plan identification of industrial control networks whose loss of integrity, exploitation, or dysfunction would have debilitating effects on national security, along with risk mitigation measures such as parallel services or hardening.
rule_text_technical: The plan required under subsection (a)(1) shall identify industrial control networks for which a loss of internet connectivity, a loss of network integrity or availability, an exploitation of a system connected to the network, or another failure, disruption, corruption, or dysfunction would have a debilitating effect on security, economic security, defense readiness, or public health or safety, and shall identify risk mitigation measures including parallel services, stand-alone analog services, or hardening of the industrial control network.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You (President) must identify in the Continuity of the Economy Plan critical economic sectors for which preservation of data in a protected, verified, and uncorrupted status is required for quick recovery after a significant event.
rule_text_technical: The plan shall identify critical economic sectors for which the preservation of data in a protected, verified, and uncorrupted status would be required for the quick recovery of the economy of the United States in the face of a significant disruption following a significant event.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Central government oversight bodies must ensure that financial assistance information is published in accordance with applicable data protection law, including identification of recipients to the extent practicable while protecting personally identifiable information.
rule_text_technical: For each assistance listing under which Federal financial assistance is provided, information shall be published consistent with existing law relating to the protection of personally identifiable information, including the identification of each award and, to the extent practicable, the name of each direct or indirect recipient.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for semiconductor assistance programs must not approve financial assistance applications from entities determined to be foreign entities of concern.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary may not approve an application for financial assistance under this section if the Secretary determines that the covered entity is a foreign entity of concern, as defined to include entities owned or controlled by adversary governments, terrorist organizations, sanctioned persons, or those convicted of espionage or export control violations.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministry responsible for technology incentives must recover the full award if the recipient knowingly engages in joint research or technology licensing with a foreign entity of concern relating to a technology product that raises national security concerns.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary shall recover the full amount of an award if, during the applicable term, the covered entity knowingly engages in any joint research or technology licensing effort with a foreign entity of concern that relates to a technology or product that raises national security concerns, as determined by the Secretary and communicated to the covered entity before engaging in such joint research or technology licensing.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: Defense and security agencies must establish a public-private partnership to incentivize the development and production of measurably secure microelectronics—including integrated circuits, logic, memory, and packaging—for defense, intelligence, and critical infrastructure use.
rule_text_technical: The Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall establish a public-private partnership to incentivize formation of consortia of companies to ensure development and production of measurably secure microelectronics, including integrated circuits, logic devices, memory, and supporting packaging and testing practices, for the Department of Defense, the intelligence community, critical infrastructure sectors, and other national security applications.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You (consortium participant) must include management processes to identify and mitigate supply chain security risks and provide microelectronic components consistent with measurably secure supply chain and operational security standards.
rule_text_technical: A participant in a consortium formed with incentives under this section shall include management processes to identify and mitigate supply chain security risks, and shall be capable of providing microelectronic components that are consistent with applicable measurably secure supply chain and operational security standards established under section 224(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: The lead government ministries responsible for defense and intelligence must periodically evaluate consortium participants for foreign ownership, control, or influence by a foreign entity of concern.
rule_text_technical: Companies participating in consortia formed with incentives under this section shall be evaluated periodically for foreign ownership, control, or influence by a foreign entity of concern.

first_instance.law_name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020

instances.notes: Rule introduced in National AI Initiative Act (2020) (United States, 2021-01-01).

rule_text: You must ensure that products with digital elements meet the essential cybersecurity requirements in Part I of Annex I before making them available on the market, assuming proper installation, maintenance, and use.
rule_text_technical: Products with digital elements shall be made available on the market only where they meet the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I, provided they are properly installed, maintained, used for their intended purpose or under reasonably foreseeable conditions, and necessary security updates have been installed.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must ensure that the processes you put in place as a manufacturer comply with the essential cybersecurity vulnerability-handling requirements in Part II of Annex I.
rule_text_technical: Products with digital elements shall be made available on the market only where the processes put in place by the manufacturer comply with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part II of Annex I.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: As a manufacturer, you must ensure that any product with digital elements you place on the market has been designed, developed, and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Part I of Annex I.
rule_text_technical: When placing a product with digital elements on the market, manufacturers shall ensure that it has been designed, developed and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must document the cybersecurity risk assessment, update it during the support period, and analyse risks based on the product's intended purpose, foreseeable use, and conditions of use.
rule_text_technical: The cybersecurity risk assessment shall be documented and updated as appropriate during the support period and shall comprise at least an analysis of cybersecurity risks based on intended purpose, reasonably foreseeable use, and conditions of use, including the operational environment and assets to be protected.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must include the cybersecurity risk assessment in the technical documentation when placing the product on the market, and provide clear justification where certain essential cybersecurity requirements are not applicable.
rule_text_technical: When placing a product on the market, the manufacturer shall include the cybersecurity risk assessment in the technical documentation required under Article 31 and Annex VII; where certain essential cybersecurity requirements are not applicable, a clear justification shall be included.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must exercise due diligence when integrating third-party components, including free and open-source components, to ensure they do not compromise the product's cybersecurity.
rule_text_technical: Manufacturers shall exercise due diligence when integrating components sourced from third parties so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product, including when integrating free and open-source software components not made available in the course of commercial activity.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: If you identify a vulnerability in a component (including open-source) integrated in your product, you must report it to the component's maintainer, address and remediate it, and share fixes where developed.
rule_text_technical: Upon identifying a vulnerability in a component integrated in the product, manufacturers shall report the vulnerability to the person or entity manufacturing or maintaining the component, address and remediate it pursuant to Part II of Annex I, and share relevant code or documentation, where appropriate in machine-readable format.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must systematically document relevant cybersecurity aspects of your products, including vulnerabilities you become aware of and information from third parties, and update the risk assessment as needed.
rule_text_technical: Manufacturers shall systematically document, proportionate to the nature and cybersecurity risks, relevant cybersecurity aspects concerning the products, including vulnerabilities and any relevant third-party information, and shall update the cybersecurity risk assessment where applicable.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: You must ensure that vulnerabilities in your product (including its components) are handled effectively during the support period in accordance with Part II of Annex I, and the support period must be at least five years unless the product's expected use is shorter.
rule_text_technical: Manufacturers shall ensure that, when placing a product on the market and for the support period, vulnerabilities are handled effectively in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Part II of Annex I. The support period shall reflect expected product use, considering reasonable user expectations, product nature, and relevant Union law, and shall be at least five years unless expected use is shorter.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: When procuring products with digital elements, Member States must ensure that compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Annex I, including effective vulnerability handling, is taken into consideration in the procurement process.
rule_text_technical: Without prejudice to Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, where products with digital elements falling within the scope of this Regulation are procured, Member States shall ensure compliance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I, including manufacturers' ability to handle vulnerabilities effectively, is taken into consideration in the procurement process.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Cyber Resilience Act (2024) (European Union, 2024-10-10).

rule_text: At trade fairs, exhibitions, demonstrations, or similar events, you may present non-compliant products only if they bear a visible sign clearly indicating non-compliance and are not made available on the market until compliant.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall not prevent the presentation or use at trade fairs, exhibitions, demonstrations or similar events of products with digital elements not complying with this Regulation, including prototypes, provided the product is presented with a visible sign clearly indicating non-compliance and that it is not made available on the market until compliant.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on Cybersecurity Requirements for Products with Digital Elements
