rule_text_technical: An information sharing agreement must be in writing, specify the purpose, set out information referred to in section 146, contain operational overview, specify privacy safeguards, identify the public sector agency responsible for complaints involving private sector parties, state every party will give reasonable assistance to identify the responsible agency, and where applicable designate the lead agency and class of agencies.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before recommending approval of an information sharing agreement, the Minister must be satisfied that it facilitates a public service, that information shared is no more than necessary, that privacy is not unreasonably impinged, that benefits outweigh costs, and that conflicts with other laws are addressed.
rule_text_technical: Before recommending an Order in Council under section 145(1), the relevant Minister must be satisfied that the agreement will facilitate provision of a public service, the type and quantity of personal information shared is no more than necessary, the agreement does not unreasonably impinge on privacy and contains adequate safeguards, benefits outweigh costs, and any conflicts with other enactments are appropriately addressed.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before concluding an information sharing agreement, you must consult and invite submissions from the Commissioner, representatives of affected individuals, and other relevant persons.
rule_text_technical: Parties proposing to enter into an information sharing agreement must, before the agreement is concluded, consult and invite submissions from the Commissioner, persons representing the interests of classes of individuals whose information will be shared, persons representing classes of agencies, and other persons the parties consider should be consulted, and have regard to those submissions.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before taking adverse action against an individual based on personal information shared under an information sharing agreement, you must give written notice describing the action and information, and allow 10 working days to dispute its correctness.
rule_text_technical: A party to an approved information sharing agreement must give written notice to an individual before taking adverse action based wholly or partly on personal information shared under the agreement, with details of the proposed adverse action and the information, and stating the individual has 10 working days from receipt to dispute correctness.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you are a lead agency for an approved information sharing agreement, you must make the agreement publicly available free of charge in your office and on the internet, and report on its operation as required.
rule_text_technical: A lead agency for an approved information sharing agreement must make a copy of the agreement available for inspection free of charge at its head office on any working day and accessible free of charge on an internet site, prepare a report on the agreement's operation at intervals required by the Commissioner, and carry out other responsibilities under this Part.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Specified accessing agencies may access identity information held by holder agencies only for the purpose specified in Schedule 3 opposite the accessing agency's name.
rule_text_technical: An accessing agency may, for the purpose specified in the second column of Schedule 3 opposite the agency's name, have access to an individual's identity information held by a holder agency specified in the third column of that schedule.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you are an accessing agency, your annual report must include details of the operation of identity information access provisions.
rule_text_technical: The chief executive of an accessing agency must include in every annual report prepared for the purposes of section 43 of the Public Finance Act 1989 details of the operation of this Part and Schedule 3.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not disclose personal information under an authorised information matching programme except in accordance with a written agreement reflecting the information matching rules.
rule_text_technical: Personal information held by an agency may be disclosed to another agency under an authorised information matching programme only in accordance with a written agreement that is entered into between the agencies and includes provisions reflecting the information matching rules or no less onerous provisions.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you take adverse action based on a discrepancy from an authorised information matching programme, you must commence the action within 12 months of receiving the discrepancy information.
rule_text_technical: If an agency decides to take adverse action against an individual on the basis of a discrepancy produced by an authorised information matching programme, the adverse action must be commenced not later than 12 months after the date the agency received or derived information from the programme that gave rise to the discrepancy, subject to extensions.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Before taking adverse action based on a discrepancy from an authorised information matching programme, you must give the individual written notice with details and a 5-working-day period to show cause.
rule_text_technical: A specified agency must not take adverse action against an individual on the basis of a discrepancy produced by an authorised information matching programme unless it has given the individual written notice specifying the discrepancy and proposed adverse action, stating the individual has 5 working days from receipt to show cause, and until those 5 working days expire.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you are involved in an authorised information matching programme, you must report to the Commissioner when required, including on costs, benefits, difficulties, audits, and operational details.
rule_text_technical: An agency involved in an authorised information matching programme must report to the Commissioner when required, including on actual costs and benefits, operational difficulties, internal audits, dispensation of notice requirements, and detailed programme statistics.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not, as a public sector agency, disclose personal information to another public sector agency under official information laws if the information is sought solely or principally for use in an information matching programme.
rule_text_technical: Despite anything in the Official Information Act 1982 or the Local Government Official Information and Meetings Act 1987, a public sector agency must not disclose to any other public sector agency under those Acts any personal information if the information is sought solely or principally for use in an information matching programme.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not, without reasonable excuse, fail or refuse to comply with a transfer prohibition notice, or face a fine of up to $10,000.
rule_text_technical: Every person who, without reasonable excuse, fails or refuses to comply with a transfer prohibition notice commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must appoint one or more privacy officers responsible for encouraging IPP compliance, handling requests, working with the Commissioner, and ensuring agency compliance with the Act.
rule_text_technical: An agency must appoint as privacy officers one or more individuals (within or outside the agency) whose responsibilities include encouraging compliance with the IPPs, dealing with requests under the Act, working with the Commissioner on investigations, and ensuring the agency complies with the Act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both require designation of an individual accountable for data protection compliance, but the Philippine DPA adds a disclosure obligation to data subjects upon request, which the NZ rule does not explicitly include.

Both require appointment of a privacy/data protection officer responsible for handling complaints, liaising with the supervisory authority, and advising on compliance, independently drafted with the same substantive functions.

Both assign compliance advisory, staff capacity-building, and supervisory functions to a designated privacy/data protection officer, though Kenya's DPA also specifically includes advising on impact assessments and cooperating with the Data Commissioner.

Both require appointment of a privacy/data protection officer responsible for compliance, handling data subject requests, and acting as contact point with regulators, though Egypt's rule adds regular evaluation duties.

Both require designating a privacy/data protection officer responsible for compliance, but the NZ Act specifies broader duties (handling requests, working with Commissioner) while Brunei's rule focuses narrowly on designation responsibility.

Both require designation of a responsible person for privacy/data protection compliance, but Quebec's rule specifically designates the highest-authority person in a public body, while NZ requires appointment of one or more privacy officers with defined functions.

Nigeria's DPO appointment obligation shares the same underlying concept as New Zealand's privacy officer requirement, but differs in threshold (Nigeria limits mandatory appointment to controllers of major importance or those conducting large-scale systematic processing), scope, and binding legal context.

Both require appointment of a Data Protection/Privacy Officer with relevant expertise, but Pakistan's rule specifically ties mandatory appointment to a 'significant data controller' designation or large-scale processing threshold, adding a regulatory trigger absent in the New Zealand provision.

Both require appointment of one or more privacy/data protection officers responsible for compliance, though Malaysia's provision is framed as accountability to the controller and applies specifically to data controllers.

rule_text: You must supply the Commissioner with your privacy officer's contact details and other reasonably required information about the personal information you hold when requested.
rule_text_technical: For the purpose of enabling the Commissioner to respond to public inquiries about personal information held by an agency, the Commissioner may require an agency to supply the name and contact details of the agency's privacy officer and any other information the Commissioner reasonably requires in relation to personal information held by the agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both require publishing/supplying the privacy/data protection officer's contact details to the relevant authority, but Kenya also requires publication on the organisation's website and communication to the Data Commissioner specifically.

Both require making contact information for the designated privacy officer available, but NZ requires supplying details to the Commissioner while Brunei requires making business contact information available to the public.

rule_text: Acts or omissions by your employees, agents, or members are treated as your acts for the purposes of this Act, subject to limited defences.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of this Act, anything done or omitted by a person as an employee of another is treated as being done or omitted by both, anything done or omitted by an agent of another is treated as done or omitted by both unless without express or implied authority, and anything done or omitted by a member of an agency is treated as done or omitted by both, unless without authority.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You (the Privacy Commissioner) may share information or documents held in the course of your functions with overseas privacy enforcement authorities where it will assist that authority's functions or enable reciprocal assistance.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may provide to an overseas privacy enforcement authority information or copies of documents held in relation to the performance of the Commissioner's functions where the Commissioner considers it may assist the authority or enable reciprocal provision of related information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must impose appropriate conditions when sharing information with an overseas privacy enforcement authority, including conditions on storage, use, access, copying, return, or disposal.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may impose any conditions considered appropriate in relation to the provision of information or documents to an overseas privacy enforcement authority, including conditions related to storage, use, access, copying, return, or disposal.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You (the Commissioner) must not make adverse comments about any person in a report or statement under this Act unless that person has been given an opportunity to be heard.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner must not, in any report or statement made pursuant to this Act or the Crown Entities Act 2004, make any comment adverse to any person unless that person has been given an opportunity to be heard.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may avoid liability for an employee's privacy breach if you can prove you took reasonably practicable steps to prevent the employee from doing the act.
rule_text_technical: In proceedings under this Act, it is a defence for an employer to prove that they took such steps as were reasonably practicable to prevent the employee from doing the act or any similar act.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not impersonate or falsely pretend to act under the authority of an individual to obtain access to, use, alter, or destroy that individual's personal information.
rule_text_technical: A person commits an offence if they mislead an agency by impersonating an individual or falsely pretending to be or act under the authority of an individual for the purpose of obtaining access to, or having used, altered, or destroyed, that individual's personal information.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not destroy any document containing personal information knowing that an access or correction request has been made for that information.
rule_text_technical: A person commits an offence if they destroy any document containing personal information knowing that a request has been made in respect of that information under subpart 1 of Part 4.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both prohibit destroying or altering records containing personal data with intent to evade an access or correction request, reflecting the same substantive obligation though drafted differently and in different statutory contexts.

Both prohibit unlawful destruction or alteration of personal data, but Tanzania's rule is broader, also covering deletion, misleading, concealment, and alteration, while NZ focuses on destruction to frustrate access requests.

rule_text: You are not required to comply with the mandatory privacy breach notification regime for breaches that occurred before 1 December 2020, even if those breaches continue after that date.
rule_text_technical: The provisions of subpart 1 of Part 6 (notifiable privacy breaches) do not apply to a notifiable privacy breach that occurred before the commencement day (1 December 2020) even if it continues after that day.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must take all reasonable steps (which may include public notification) to ensure that individuals affected by an authorised information matching programme are notified of the programme, unless notification would frustrate the programme's objective.
rule_text_technical: Agencies involved in an authorised information matching programme must take all reasonable steps to ensure that affected individuals are notified, except where notification would be likely to frustrate the objective of the programme.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not use unique identifiers as part of an authorised information matching programme unless their use is essential to the success of the programme.
rule_text_technical: Except as provided in any other enactment, unique identifiers may not be used as part of any authorised information matching programme unless their use is essential to the success of the programme.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you are the lead agency for an authorised information matching programme, you must establish and maintain detailed technical standards governing data integrity, matching techniques, controls, and security features.
rule_text_technical: The agency primarily responsible for an authorised information matching programme must establish and maintain detailed technical standards covering: integrity of information matched (key terms, relevance, timeliness, completeness); matching techniques (algorithm, unique identifiers, definitions, recognising matches); controls for continued integrity and validity; and security features minimising and auditing access.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must record the technical standards in a written Technical Standards Report, distribute it to all involved agencies, and forward copies (and any variations) to the Privacy Commissioner.
rule_text_technical: Technical standards must be incorporated in a written Technical Standards Report held by all agencies involved in the programme; variations may be made via Variation Report appended to the original; and the preparing agency must forward the report and any variations to the Commissioner.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must comply with the Technical Standards Report (including any variations) and any direction by the Commissioner to vary the standards.
rule_text_technical: The Commissioner may direct that a Technical Standards Report be varied, and that direction must be complied with by the agency that prepared the report; every agency involved in an authorised information matching programme must comply with the requirements of the associated Technical Standards Report.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must establish reasonable procedures to confirm the validity of discrepancies revealed by an information matching programme before relying on them to take action against an individual, unless there are reasonable grounds to believe the results are unlikely to be in error.
rule_text_technical: Agencies involved in an authorised information matching programme must establish reasonable procedures for confirming the validity of discrepancies before relying on them as a basis for action in respect of an individual, except where the agencies consider there are reasonable grounds to believe the results are not likely to be in error having regard to consistency in content and context.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both rules restrict purely automated decision-making affecting individuals, but the Senegal law broadly prohibits basing judicial or legally significant decisions solely on automated personal data processing, while the NZ rule specifically requires validation of discrepancies in information matching programmes before relying on them — different scope, context, and obligation structure.

rule_text: If your validation procedure involves contacting the affected individual rather than checking against source information, you must notify the individual that no such source check has been made and explain the discrepancy examination procedure.
rule_text_technical: Where confirmation procedures do not take the form of checking results against the source information but instead involve direct communication with the affected individual, the agency seeking to rely on the discrepancy must notify the individual that no source check has been made and include an explanation of the procedures involved in examining the discrepancy.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must destroy as soon as practicable any information matching information that does not reveal a discrepancy.
rule_text_technical: Information matching information held by an agency that does not reveal a discrepancy must be destroyed as soon as practicable by the agency.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must destroy information matching information revealing a discrepancy within 60 working days of becoming aware of the discrepancy unless you decide to take adverse action against an individual based on it.
rule_text_technical: An agency holding information matching information that reveals a discrepancy must destroy that information within 60 working days after becoming aware of the discrepancy unless it decides to take adverse action against any individual on the basis of the discrepancy.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: If you take adverse action based on a discrepancy, you must destroy the information matching information as soon as practicable after it is no longer required.
rule_text_technical: An agency that decides to take adverse action against an individual on the basis of a discrepancy must destroy the information as soon as practicable after the information is no longer required.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You must not link or merge information used in an authorised information matching programme so as to create a new separate permanent register or databank about individuals subject to the programme.
rule_text_technical: Agencies involved in an authorised information matching programme must not permit the information used to be linked or merged in such a way that a new separate permanent register or databank is created about all or any of the individuals whose information has been subject to the programme.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may maintain a register of individuals warranting further inquiry following a matching discrepancy, but only for as long as necessary to conduct inquiries or take adverse action.
rule_text_technical: An agency may maintain a register of individuals in respect of whom further inquiries are warranted following a discrepancy, but information may only be maintained for so long as necessary to enable inquiries to be carried out, and no longer than necessary to enable adverse action to be taken.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: You may maintain a register to exclude individuals from being selected for investigation, but it must contain only the minimum information necessary for that purpose.
rule_text_technical: An agency may maintain a register for the purpose of excluding individuals from being selected for investigation, but that register may contain only the minimum amount of information necessary for that purpose.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Organizations must limit personal data collection to lawful and fair means and shall obtain explicit consent from data subjects before collecting their personal information, except where legally exempted.
rule_text_technical: There should be limits to the collection of personal data and any such data should be obtained by lawful and fair means and, where appropriate, with the knowledge or consent of the data subject.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

rule_text: Organizations shall maintain a comprehensive policy of openness about developments, practices, and policies regarding personal data, and must provide accessible means for individuals to establish the existence, nature, and main purposes of personal data processing and the identity of the data controller.
rule_text_technical: There should be a general policy of openness about developments, practices and policies with respect to personal data, with means readily available of establishing the existence and nature of personal data, the main purposes of their use, and the identity and usual residence of the data controller.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both rules establish a right to information about how personal data is processed, but Costa Rica's provision is narrower and more specific—granting individuals a right to know the system/program/method/process used—while New Zealand's openness principle is broader and more general in scope.

rule_text: As a data controller, you are required to maintain accountability for full compliance with all measures that implement the OECD privacy principles.
rule_text_technical: A data controller should be accountable for complying with measures which give effect to the principles stated in the OECD Guidelines.

first_instance.law_name: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand, 2020-06-30).

Both establish that the data controller bears responsibility for compliance with data protection obligations, reflecting the same accountability principle though one is binding statute and the other references OECD principles.

rule_text: You must use technologies that ensure, to the extent practicable, that images produced by photo speed violation monitoring systems do not identify the driver, passengers, or contents of the vehicle.
rule_text_technical: Photo speed violation monitoring system programs operated by the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority and the New York State Bridge Authority shall utilize necessary technologies to ensure, to the extent practicable, that photographs, microphotographs, videotape or other recorded images shall not include images that identify the driver, passengers, or contents of the vehicle.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must treat photographs, microphotographs, videotape and other recorded images prepared under the photo speed violation monitoring authority as exempt from public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Law.
rule_text_technical: Subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public officers law is amended to add exemptions for records that are photographs, microphotographs, videotape or other recorded images prepared under authority of sections 1111-h and 1111-i of the vehicle and traffic law.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: This article defines AI, generative AI, AI models, AI companions, operators, emotional recognition algorithms, and users for the purpose of regulating AI companion systems in New York.
rule_text_technical: Section 1700 sets forth definitions of 'artificial intelligence,' 'generative artificial intelligence,' 'AI model,' 'AI companion,' 'operator,' 'person,' 'emotional recognition algorithms,' and 'user' as used in Article 47 of the general business law.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a business making automatic renewal or continuous service offers, present material terms clearly and conspicuously, including costs, frequency of charges, and the deadline by which the consumer must act to stop further charges, before consent is obtained.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful for any business making an automatic renewal or continuous service offer to fail to present to the consumer, in a clear and conspicuous manner, the material terms of any automatic renewal offer terms or continuous service offer terms, including the amount of costs, frequency of charges, and the deadline by date or frequency by which the consumer must act to prevent or stop further charges, before billing information has been requested.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must provide an acknowledgment of automatic renewal or continuous service offer terms in a manner capable of being retained by the consumer, including a clear cancellation mechanism at least as easy to use as the acceptance mechanism.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful to fail to provide an acknowledgment of the terms of the automatic renewal, continuous service offer, or increased price at or immediately following acceptance in a manner that is capable of being retained by the consumer, including a clear and conspicuous disclosure of the cancellation mechanism that must be at least as easy to access and use as the mechanism by which the consumer provided consent, and contact information including a toll-free telephone number, email address, and web address.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must provide consumers with the option to cancel automatic renewals at any time through the same medium by which they accepted the offer, including options like cancellation via toll-free number, business email, or a 'cancel' button on the website header.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful to fail to provide the consumer with the option to cancel at any time through the same medium by which the consumer accepted the automatic renewal, continuous service offer, or any price increase, which may include a direct connection to a live or automated process, an option to cancel through email, or a 'cancel' button or link clearly displayed on the header of the business website.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must not impose unreasonable or unlawful conditions, refuse to acknowledge, or delay cancellation requested by a consumer.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful to impose unreasonable or unlawful conditions upon, refuse to acknowledge, or delay cancellation requested by a consumer.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must notify consumers of upcoming automatic renewal charges at least 15 days but not more than 45 days before the cancellation deadline for offers with initial paid terms of one year or longer, with instructions on how to cancel.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful to fail to notify a consumer of an automatic renewal or continuous service charge for an automatic renewal or continuous service offer with an initial paid term of one year or longer at least fifteen days before, but not more than forty-five days before, the cancellation deadline. Such notice shall include instructions on how to cancel and be delivered in the manner selected by the consumer.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must provide consumers with clear and conspicuous notice of any material change to automatic renewal terms, including price increases, at least five business days prior to the change.
rule_text_technical: It shall be unlawful to fail to provide a consumer who has accepted an automatic renewal or continuous service offer with a clear and conspicuous notice of any material change to the terms, including any previously undisclosed price increases, at least five business days prior to the date of the change.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must not, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, engage in any unfair, deceptive or abusive act or practice or misrepresent or omit material information in connection with buy-now-pay-later loans.
rule_text_technical: No buy-now-pay-later lender shall employ any scheme, device, or artifice to defraud or mislead a borrower; engage in any unfair, deceptive or abusive act or practice toward any person or misrepresent or omit any material information in connection with buy-now-pay-later loans, including misrepresenting the amount, nature or terms of any fee or payment due on the loan.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must not, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, provide inaccurate information to a consumer reporting agency.
rule_text_technical: No buy-now-pay-later lender shall provide inaccurate information to a consumer reporting agency.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, clearly and conspicuously disclose loan terms including cost, repayment schedule, and whether transactions will be reported to a credit reporting agency, in compliance with federal Regulation Z.
rule_text_technical: A buy-now-pay-later lender shall disclose to consumers the terms of buy-now-pay-later loans, including the cost, such as interest and fees, repayment schedule, whether the transaction will or will not be reported to a credit reporting agency, and other material conditions, in a clear and conspicuous manner. Disclosures shall comply with applicable federal regulations, including regulation Z of title I of the Consumer Credit Protection Act.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, make a reasonable determination of a consumer's ability to repay before providing a loan, and must not use the credit characteristics of the borrower's social network or any group score in that determination.
rule_text_technical: A buy-now-pay-later lender shall make a reasonable determination that the consumer has the ability to repay the buy-now-pay-later loan. No licensee shall collect, evaluate, report, or maintain in the file on a borrower the credit worthiness, credit standing, or credit capacity of members of the borrower's social network for purposes of determining the credit worthiness of the borrower; the average credit worthiness of members of the borrower's social network; or any group score that is not the borrower's own.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, obtain a consumer's consent before using, selling, or sharing their data outside the making of a particular loan, and must clearly disclose how the data may be used and how consent may later be withdrawn.
rule_text_technical: A buy-now-pay-later lender may use, sell, or share the data of a consumer, other than in connection with the making of a particular buy-now-pay-later loan to the consumer, only with the consumer's consent. The lender shall disclose to a consumer in a clear and conspicuous manner how such consumer's data may be used, shared, or sold before obtaining consent and shall also disclose how the consumer may subsequently withdraw consent. The lender shall maintain policies and procedures regarding its use, sale, and sharing of consumers' data.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a buy-now-pay-later lender, keep books, accounts, and records sufficient for the superintendent to determine compliance, and preserve them for at least six years after final entry on a loan.
rule_text_technical: A buy-now-pay-later lender shall keep and use in its business such books, accounts and records as will enable the superintendent to determine whether such lender is complying with the provisions of this article. Every lender shall preserve such books, accounts and records for at least six years after making the final entry in respect to any buy-now-pay-later loan recorded therein.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a pharmacy benefit manager, publish an annual report on your website by July 1 disclosing aggregated rebates received from drug manufacturers, amounts retained vs. passed on to health plans, and detailed contract-level data.
rule_text_technical: Not later than July first of each year, a pharmacy benefit manager required to be licensed under this article shall publish a report on its website containing, for the immediately preceding calendar year, aggregated dollar amounts of rebates and other payments received from drug manufacturers, portions retained or passed to health plans, and for each rebate contract: contracting parties, dates, drug names and NDCs, terms regarding formulary placement, prescription volumes, rebate amounts retained, and other compensation paid.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: If you are a broker-dealer, investment adviser, or qualified individual and reasonably believe financial exploitation of an eligible adult has occurred or is being attempted, you may promptly notify adult protective services and/or law enforcement.
rule_text_technical: If a broker-dealer, investment adviser, or qualified individual reasonably believes financial exploitation of an eligible adult has occurred, has been attempted, or is being attempted, such broker-dealer, investment adviser, or qualified individual may promptly notify the adult protective services and/or law enforcement.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a broker-dealer or investment adviser, provide access to or copies of records relevant to suspected financial exploitation of an eligible adult to adult protective services, agencies of competent jurisdiction, or law enforcement.
rule_text_technical: A broker-dealer or investment adviser shall provide access to or copies of records that are relevant to the suspected or attempted financial exploitation of an eligible adult to adult protective services, an agency of competent jurisdiction, and law enforcement. All records made available shall be considered confidential records and shall not be available for examination by the public.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must, as a banking institution, provide access to or copies of records relevant to suspected financial exploitation of an eligible adult to adult protective services, agencies of competent jurisdiction, or law enforcement.
rule_text_technical: A banking institution shall provide access to or copies of records that are relevant to the suspected or attempted financial exploitation of an eligible adult to adult protective services, an agency of competent jurisdiction, and law enforcement, either as part of a notification or at the request of adult protective services, a law enforcement agency, or an agency of competent jurisdiction. All records made available shall be considered confidential records and shall not be available for examination by the public.

first_instance.law_name: New York A3008 — Personalized Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure and AI Companion Regulation

instances.notes: Rule introduced in New York A3008 (Algorithmic Pricing & AI Companions Act) (New York, 2025-05-09).

rule_text: You must establish an independent AI Market Surveillance Chamber at the Federal Network Agency for high-risk AI systems used in law enforcement, border management, justice/democracy, and those falling under Annex III points 6, 7, and 8.
rule_text_technical: An independent AI Market Surveillance Chamber pursuant to § 4 shall be established at the Federal Network Agency for market surveillance of high-risk AI systems under Annex III point 1 (used for law enforcement, border management, justice/democracy) and Annex III points 6, 7 and 8 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must have the German Accreditation Body assess and supervise conformity assessment bodies seated in Germany that perform conformity assessments for high-risk AI systems under Annex III point 1.
rule_text_technical: Assessment and supervision of conformity assessment bodies pursuant to Article 3(21) seated in Germany carrying out conformity assessments for high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III point 1 shall be the responsibility of the German Accreditation Body (Deutsche Akkreditierungsstelle).

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

Both rules designate a national accreditation body to assess conformity assessment bodies under AI Act Article 28(2), but Norway names Norsk akkreditering specifically for the EEA context while Germany names the German Accreditation Body (DAkkS) for Germany-seated bodies.

rule_text: You must, as the AI Market Surveillance Chamber, submit an annual activity report to the Bundestag by 31 March of the year following the reporting year.
rule_text_technical: The AI Market Surveillance Chamber shall submit an annual activity report to the Bundestag, drawn up for the first time for 2026 and transmitted by 31 March of the year following the reporting year.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as the competent market surveillance authority, notify risks despite compliance of an AI system without undue delay via the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health.
rule_text_technical: Notification of risks despite compliance of an AI system pursuant to Article 82(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 shall be made by the competent market surveillance authority without undue delay via the BAuA.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must establish a central complaints mechanism that receives complaints, forwards them to the appropriate regulatory authority responsible for market surveillance or enforcement, and notifies complainants about which authority is handling their case.
rule_text_technical: The central complaints body shall forward complaints to the competent market surveillance authority under § 2(2)–(8) or to authorities/public bodies competent under Article 77(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, and inform the complainant of the forwarding without prejudice to GDPR information duties.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as the Federal Network Agency, set up a complaints management system in accordance with the requirements of the Barrier-Free Information Technology Regulation.
rule_text_technical: To perform tasks as central complaints body, the Bundesnetzagentur shall set up a complaints management system in accordance with the Barrier-Free Information Technology Regulation.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Before issuing a measure against a subordinate federal authority for an AI Regulation infringement, the market surveillance authority must give the competent legal or technical supervisory authority the opportunity to comment, except in cases of imminent danger or compelling public interest.
rule_text_technical: Before the market surveillance authority issues a measure against a subordinate federal authority for an infringement of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the competent legal or technical supervisory authority shall be given the opportunity to comment, unless there is imminent danger, immediate measures are necessary in the public interest, or a compelling public interest stands in the way; this does not apply where the public body is a law enforcement authority.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You may, as a competent authority, exchange information including personal data and trade/business secrets among yourselves where strictly necessary to perform tasks under the EU AI Regulation and the Act.
rule_text_technical: Authorities referred to in paragraphs 1–4 may exchange information including personal data and trade and business secrets in so far as strictly necessary for the performance of their tasks pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and this Act, subject to evidence-use prohibitions and mutual legal assistance provisions.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Financial regulators and their employees or contractors must not disclose or use confidential information obtained through regulatory activities without authorization, including after employment or engagement ends.
rule_text_technical: Persons employed by or commissioned by BaFin must not, without authorisation, disclose or use facts coming to their knowledge whose confidentiality is in the interest of obligated persons, competent authorities, or third parties (especially trade and business secrets), even after leaving service; recipients of such facts are subject to equivalent obligations and foreign bodies must have equivalent confidentiality duties.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as the AI market surveillance authority and the cybersecurity market surveillance authority, cooperate, exchange information on suspected non-compliance with cybersecurity requirements, and draw up joint specifications for examining cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems.
rule_text_technical: Market surveillance authorities under this Act and the authority designated under Article 52(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 shall cooperate, share information on suspected non-compliance of high-risk AI systems with cybersecurity requirements under Article 13(3)(b)(ii) and Article 15(1) and (5), and draw up joint specifications for examining those cybersecurity requirements.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Data covered by particularly worthy interests of secrecy of public bodies (such as security authorities) may not, in principle, be collected or processed by market surveillance authorities, except where the processing interest prevails (e.g., concrete indications of particularly serious infringement).
rule_text_technical: Where public bodies, particularly security authorities, have particularly protection-worthy interests of secrecy, data covered thereby shall not generally be collected or further processed within the meaning of Article 4(2) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, unless the market surveillance authority's interest exceptionally prevails (e.g., concrete indications of particularly serious infringement of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689).

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: The fiscal authority may disclose data subject to fiscal secrecy to the market surveillance authority only upon reasoned request, limited to the necessary extent and only where necessary for performance of powers under the AI Regulation.
rule_text_technical: The fiscal authority shall disclose data subject to fiscal secrecy to the market surveillance authority only at the latter's reasoned request, limited to the necessary extent, and only where necessary for the market surveillance authority to perform its powers under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Objections and actions against market surveillance decisions under this Act do not have suspensive effect; measures of the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority and threatened or imposed coercive measures are immediately enforceable.
rule_text_technical: Objection and action against decisions of market surveillance shall not have suspensive effect; measures of the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority under this Act, including the threat and imposition of coercive measures, are immediately enforceable, deviating from § 80(1) VwGO.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as the Federal Network Agency providing advisory tasks on AI classification to public bodies, conclude an administrative agreement with the competent ministry covering cost assumption, and publish the essential considerations of the advisory result.
rule_text_technical: Performance of advisory tasks pursuant to § 12 sentence 2 point 2 requires an administrative agreement between the Bundesnetzagentur and the competent federal/Land ministry regulating assumption of financial and staff costs; the Bundesnetzagentur shall publish the essential considerations of its advisory results.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as the Federal Network Agency, grant priority access to the AI regulatory sandbox to research institutions, universities, and their spin-offs with EU seat that meet the requirements and where access facilitates Union market access of AI systems from applied research.
rule_text_technical: Beyond Article 62(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the Bundesnetzagentur shall grant priority access to the AI regulatory sandbox to research institutions, universities and their spin-offs with seat or branch in the EU, in so far as they fulfil requirements/selection criteria under Article 58(1) implementing acts and access facilitates/accelerates Union market access of AI systems from applied research/development projects.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must, as a provider or prospective provider, submit the plan for testing high-risk AI systems under real-world conditions to the competent market surveillance authority before placing on the market or putting into service, and obtain approval (deemed granted after 30 days of silence).
rule_text_technical: Before providers or prospective providers test Annex III high-risk AI systems under real-world conditions, they must submit the test plan to the competent market surveillance authority; testing must occur before placing on the market or putting into service; the authority approves where Article 60(4) requirements are met; approval is deemed granted where no response is received within 30 days of receipt.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: You must provide a clear explanation to any person affected by a high-risk AI system's decision, covering how the system works and why it reached that particular outcome.
rule_text_technical: Any person who, as deployer of a high-risk AI system under Article 6(2) in conjunction with Annex III points 1, 3, 4 or 5, fails to ensure that an explanation referred to in Article 86(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is given to an affected person, commits an administrative offence.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

Both rules require transparency and interpretability instructions for deployers of high-risk AI systems, with the German rule framing it as an administrative offence trigger and the Norwegian rule framing it as a design obligation, but the substantive requirement is the same EU AI Act Art. 13 transposition.

rule_text: You must not impose fines against government authorities or public bodies for administrative violations of AI governance rules.
rule_text_technical: Against authorities and other public bodies within the meaning of § 2(1) or (2) BDSG, no fines shall be imposed in cases of § 15(1) and (2) and of Article 99(3)–(5) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

Both prohibit imposing administrative fines on public authorities and bodies, but the Finnish rule enumerates a broader list of exempted entities (state authorities, enterprises, municipal bodies, wellbeing service counties) while the German rule focuses on authorities under BDSG.

rule_text: You must, as a whistleblower reporting infringements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, be protected under the Whistleblower Protection Act as the scope is extended to such infringements.
rule_text_technical: § 2(1) of the Whistleblower Protection Act is amended by inserting a new point 10 covering 'Infringements of provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689'.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: When processing social data, you must treat data protection obligations under applicable data protection law as taking precedence over other regulatory requirements in the same manner as those laws require.
rule_text_technical: § 35(2) sentence 1 SGB I is replaced so that provisions of the Second Chapter of Book Ten and other Social Code books regulate the processing of social data conclusively unless GDPR or Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 contains directly applicable legal provisions for protection of personal data in their processing.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: If a complaint is submitted to a market surveillance authority other than the BNetzA, that authority must provide the Federal Network Agency at minimum with a copy of the complaint.
rule_text_technical: Where a complaint is submitted to another market surveillance authority, that authority shall provide the Federal Network Agency at least with a copy of the complaint, so that the BNetzA obtains an overview of all complaints.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: The cybersecurity market surveillance authority must inform the competent AI market surveillance authority of suspected non-compliance with cybersecurity requirements in high-risk AI systems, providing a reasoned assessment.
rule_text_technical: The market surveillance authority designated under Article 52(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 shall inform the competent AI market surveillance authority of suspected non-compliance with cybersecurity requirements in high-risk AI systems and provide a reasoned assessment, with examination based on jointly developed specifications by BNetzA and the cybersecurity authority (and BaFin for financial undertakings).

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: The Federal Network Agency must establish a central AI service desk for providers and deployers of AI systems and other addressees of the EU AI Regulation.
rule_text_technical: The Federal Network Agency shall establish a central AI service desk for providers and deployers of AI systems and other addressees of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: In intermediate proceedings, the public prosecutor's office may discontinue administrative fine proceedings only with the consent of the market surveillance authority that issued the fine notice.
rule_text_technical: The public prosecutor's office in intermediate proceedings may discontinue proceedings only with the consent of the market surveillance authority that issued the administrative fine notice, recognising the importance of administrative fines and the independence of market surveillance.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Persons who report or disclose infringements of the EU AI Regulation must be protected under the Whistleblower Protection Act.
rule_text_technical: The Whistleblower Protection Act applies to the reporting and disclosure of infringements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, transposing Article 87 thereof and Directive (EU) 2019/1937 as amended.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: Organizations must ensure that processing of social data complies with requirements for human oversight, transparency, and risk management, and must provide individuals with the rights to access, correct, and delete their personal information.
rule_text_technical: Social data processing rules in the Tenth Book of the Social Code in conjunction with the First Book are supplemented by direct primacy of Article 10(5) and Article 59 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, alongside Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and other Union data protection law preserved under Article 2(7) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.

first_instance.law_name: Germany — Gesetz zur Durchführung der europäischen KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsgesetz — KI-MIG)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Germany KI-MIG (Germany, null).

rule_text: If you are a provider who considers an Annex III AI system not to pose high risk, you must document the assessment before placing it on the market and register it accordingly.
rule_text_technical: Where a provider considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk because it does not pose significant risk of harm, the provider must document the assessment before placing on the market or putting into service, comply with registration obligations under Article 49(2), and provide documentation upon request.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must design high-risk AI systems so they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during their use.
rule_text_technical: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use, including the ability to stop, override, or take direct control of the system.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

Both require effective human oversight of AI systems, but the Malaysia rule is more specific in naming HITL, HOTL, and HIC mechanisms as implementation approaches, whereas the Norwegian rule focuses on design for natural-person oversight of high-risk systems.

Both require human oversight and control over AI systems, but the Mauritius rule emphasizes override capability and general control while the Norwegian rule focuses on effective oversight during use of high-risk AI systems specifically.

rule_text: You must ensure high-risk AI systems achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle.
rule_text_technical: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed so as to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, performing consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must put in place a quality management system as a provider of high-risk AI systems, documented through written policies, procedures, and instructions.
rule_text_technical: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put in place a quality management system that ensures compliance with this Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions, proportionate to the size of the provider's organisation.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

Both rules require providers of high-risk AI systems to operate a quality management system under Article 17 of the EU AI Act, but the Finnish rule frames the obligation from an enforcement/administrative-penalty perspective while the Norwegian rule frames it as a direct compliance obligation.

rule_text: As a deployer of a high-risk AI system, you must take appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure use in accordance with the instructions for use and assign human oversight to competent persons.
rule_text_technical: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use, and assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training, and authority.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

Both require deployers of high-risk AI systems to take measures ensuring oversight/monitoring during use, but the Norwegian rule specifies 'appropriate technical and organizational measures' and compliance with instructions, while the Finnish rule is a narrower, more general monitoring obligation without specifying the means or standards.

rule_text: As a deployer of an emotion recognition or biometric categorization system, you must inform natural persons exposed to the system of its operation and process personal data in compliance with data protection law.
rule_text_technical: Deployers of emotion recognition systems or biometric categorisation systems shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system and process personal data in accordance with applicable data protection regulations.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: If you deploy AI systems that generate or manipulate text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, you must disclose that the text was artificially generated or manipulated.
rule_text_technical: Deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated, with exceptions for editorial review or law enforcement.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

Both require disclosure that AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest is artificially generated, independently adopted in Finland and Norway with different drafting.

rule_text: If you are a competent authority, notified body, or other person involved in enforcement, you must respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out tasks.
rule_text_technical: The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies, and any other natural or legal person involved in the application of this Regulation shall respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities, including IP rights and trade secrets.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: The government may issue regulations governing the operation of AI regulatory sandboxes pursuant to the AI Regulation.
rule_text_technical: A regulatory power is established for further regulation of AI regulatory sandboxes pursuant to AI Regulation Articles 57-61, with operations to be coordinated between Digdir, Nkom, and the Data Protection Authority.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: The government may by regulation extend the application of the AI Act to Svalbard, Jan Mayen, the continental shelf, and foreign-registered ships and aircraft in Norwegian territory.
rule_text_technical: Regulatory power is provided to extend the AI Act to Svalbard and Jan Mayen, to the continental shelf where appropriate, and to foreign-registered ships in Norwegian territorial waters and foreign-registered aircraft in Norwegian airspace.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: As a provider of a high-risk AI system, you must ensure your system meets all applicable safety and performance requirements and clearly display your name and contact information on the system or its packaging.
rule_text_technical: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall ensure that their high-risk AI systems are compliant with the requirements set out in Section 2, indicate name/registered name/trademark and contact address on the system or accompanying documentation, and have a quality management system in place.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: As an importer or distributor of a high-risk AI system, you must verify that the system bears CE marking, has the required documentation, and not place it on the market if not in conformity.
rule_text_technical: Importers shall ensure before placing a high-risk AI system on the market that it conforms to the Regulation, including CE marking, accompanying documentation, and authorised representative designation; distributors shall verify compliance similarly before making available on the market.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must comply with EU Regulation 2024/1689 (the AI Act) as it applies as Norwegian law, including the adaptations following from the EEA Agreement Annex XI and Protocol 1.
rule_text_technical: EØS-avtalen vedlegg XI (forordning (EU) 2024/1689) om fastsettelse av et harmonisert regelverk om kunstig intelligens gjelder som norsk lov med de tilpasninger som følger av vedlegg XI, protokoll 1 og avtalen for øvrig.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You may be subject to a coercive fine (running daily or as a one-off) for failing to comply with orders issued under this Act.
rule_text_technical: I pålegg gitt etter denne loven kan det fastsettes en tvangsmulkt som løper for hver dag etter utløpet av fristen for oppfylling, inntil pålegget er oppfylt; tvangsmulkten kan også fastsettes som engangsmulkt.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must have administrative fines determined by the rules in force at the time of the act, unless later legislation gives a more favourable outcome.
rule_text_technical: Reglene som gjaldt på handlingstidspunktet skal legges til grunn ved vedtak om overtredelsesgebyr; lovgivningen på tidspunktet for avgjørelsen anvendes likevel når dette fører til et gunstigere resultat for den ansvarlige.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: If a market surveillance authority concludes that an AI system you classified as non-high-risk is in fact high-risk, you must take all necessary measures to bring the system into compliance within the deadline set.
rule_text_technical: Leverandøren er forpliktet til å sikre at alle nødvendige tiltak gjennomføres for å overholde forordningens krav, og skal gjennomføre korrigerende tiltak for alle relevante KI-systemer gjort tilgjengelig på markedet i EU når markedstilsynsmyndigheten har omklassifisert systemet som høyrisiko etter artikkel 80.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must not intentionally misclassify an AI system to avoid compliance with requirements applicable to high-risk systems, and violations of this obligation are subject to financial penalties.
rule_text_technical: Leverandøren skal ilegges gebyr i samsvar med artikkel 99 hvis markedstilsynsmyndigheten kommer frem til at leverandøren ikke klassifiserte KI-systemet som et høyrisikosystem i den hensikt å omgå kravene til høyrisikosystemer i kapittel III del 2.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: Sectoral market surveillance authorities must establish procedures to receive and process serious-incident reports, including assessing whether fundamental rights are affected and notifying the relevant national bodies that supervise fundamental rights compliance.
rule_text_technical: Den enkelte sektorielle markedstilsynsmyndighet må sørge for at det etableres rutiner som oppfyller kravene til mottak av rapporter om alvorlige hendelser, inkludert vurdering av om grunnleggende rettigheter er berørt og varsling av nasjonale offentlige myndigheter som fører tilsyn med EU-regler om grunnleggende rettigheter.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).
