rule_text: If you provide a general-purpose AI model and breach the regulation, the Commission may impose fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
rule_text_technical: Kommisjonen kan ilegge gebyrer på opptil 15 millioner euro eller 3 % av den globale omsetningen ved brudd på forordningen for leverandører av KI-modeller for allmenne formål.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You may participate in a regulatory sandbox under Articles 57-61 of the AI Act as further specified in regulations, including provisions enabling reuse of personal data for new purposes when the sandbox is used for law-enforcement purposes.
rule_text_technical: Departementet kan gi forskrift om regulatoriske sandkasser etter KI-forordningen artikkel 57 til 61, herunder regulering av bruk av personopplysninger til nye formål når deltakelse skjer for rettshåndhevelsesformål.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You (as a state party) must ensure effective remedies for human-rights violations resulting from AI activities and effective complaint mechanisms to competent authorities for AI systems with significant impact on human rights.
rule_text_technical: Konvensjonen stiller krav om effektive rettsmidler for menneskerettighetsbrudd som skyldes KI-aktiviteter og at individer skal ha en effektiv mulighet til å klage på et KI-system til kompetente myndigheter, jf. artikkel 14 og 15.

first_instance.law_name: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA) (Norway, null).

rule_text: You must, as the Department of Corrections, use appropriated funds for technology modernization and the development of an information-sharing and data-technology infrastructure for public safety.
rule_text_technical: $4,097,000 each year is appropriated for technology modernization and the development of an information-sharing and data-technology infrastructure; unspent funds carry over to the next biennium.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: The designated fraud investigation authority may share active investigative data concerning insurance fraud with the supervisory authority responsible for public safety and the government agency responsible for criminal investigation.
rule_text_technical: The commissioner may share active investigative data pursuant to section 13.39 concerning insurance fraud with the commissioner of public safety and the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: Organizations must keep unemployment insurance data private but may disseminate it without consent to sector-specific regulators and other government agencies for purposes authorized under applicable law.
rule_text_technical: Data gathered under the Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Law are private data on individuals or nonpublic data and may not be disclosed except per court order or section 13.05; specified agencies including the Department of Labor and Industry, Department of Commerce, and Bureau of Criminal Apprehension may receive data for uses consistent with administration of their duties.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: You must keep paid family and medical leave data private but may share it without consent with specified agencies and contracted third parties to the extent necessary to aid in identity verification, adjudication, administration, and program evaluation.
rule_text_technical: Data collected under chapter 268B are private or nonpublic data and may be disseminated without consent to enumerated entities including contracted third parties to aid in identity verification, adjudication, administration, and evaluation of the program.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: You must, as a state agency, report all suspected fraud involving state-funded programs equaling $10,000 or more to the Financial Crimes and Fraud Section by January 15 each year.
rule_text_technical: By January 15 of each year, each state agency must report all suspected fraud incurred by the agency that involves state-funded or administered programs or services equaling $10,000 or more to the Section to be summarized in the annual report.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: You must not, as a healthcare provider, release a copy of a recording of a child victim or alleged victim of physical or sexual abuse without a court order.
rule_text_technical: A provider may not release a copy of a recording of a child victim or alleged victim of physical or sexual abuse without a court order under section 13.03, subdivision 6, or as provided in section 611A.90; this does not limit the patient's right to view or listen to the recording.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: You must, as a correctional facility administrator, report all deaths of individuals committed to the facility's custody to the commissioner within 24 hours, including required demographic information.
rule_text_technical: All facility administrators must report all deaths of individuals who died while committed to the facility's custody, regardless of where the death occurred, as soon as practicable but no later than 24 hours after receiving knowledge, including any demographic information required by the commissioner.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: The superintendent must publish an annual report on the Minnesota Fusion Center that discloses the types of surveillance and data analysis technologies it uses, such as artificial intelligence or social media analysis tools, and the commercial and governmental databases it relies on.
rule_text_technical: Pursuant to Minn. Stat. § 299C.055, the superintendent shall prepare an annual public and legislative report on the Minnesota Fusion Center disclosing, inter alia, the types of surveillance and data analysis technologies utilized (including AI or social media analysis tools) and a description of commercial and governmental databases utilized, to the extent permitted by law.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: Law enforcement may attach a mobile tracking device to a stolen vehicle without a warrant only if the owner consents or reported it stolen and the vehicle is not on private property, and the device must be removed, disabled, or covered by a warrant within 12 hours.
rule_text_technical: Under Minn. Stat. § 626A.35, subd. 2b, the prohibition on warrantless mobile tracking device installation does not apply to a stolen vehicle when the owner consents or reported the vehicle stolen and the vehicle is not on private property; within 12 hours of attachment under clause (a)(2), the agency must remove, disable, or obtain a search warrant for continued use; the device must be removed upon recovery and return to the owner; any tracking data collected after return is inadmissible.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: When attaching a tracking device to a stolen vehicle, the peace officer must prepare a report documenting the evidence relied upon, the date/time, attachment method, duration, and outcome impact, and retain it in the criminal investigation file.
rule_text_technical: Under § 626A.35, subd. 2b(e), a peace officer attaching a tracking device to a stolen vehicle pursuant to (a)(2) must prepare a report including the evidence relied upon to establish the vehicle was reported stolen, date/time of attachment, method of attachment, duration of use, and an explanation of investigative impact; the report must be retained as part of the criminal investigation file.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: By August 1 each year, the chief law enforcement officer of an agency that obtained a tracking-device search warrant under this provision must report the number obtained in the prior 12 months to the BCA superintendent.
rule_text_technical: By August 1, 2024, and each year thereafter, the chief law enforcement officer of an agency obtaining a search warrant under § 626A.35, subd. 2b(b) must notify the BCA superintendent of the number of search warrants obtained under the subdivision in the preceding 12 months; the superintendent must summarize the data in the BCA biennial report under § 299C.18.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: Police may attach a mobile tracking device to a fleeing vehicle without a warrant, but if the vehicle is not in custody within 12 hours, the device must be removed, disabled, or covered by a warrant.
rule_text_technical: Under § 626A.35, subd. 2c, the prohibition on mobile tracking devices does not apply to a fleeing motor vehicle; within 12 hours of attachment, if the vehicle is not in law enforcement custody, the agency must remove, disable, or obtain a search warrant. The device must be removed upon recovery if returned to owner; subsequent tracking data is inadmissible. The officer must prepare a report documenting evidence of fleeing, date/time, method, duration, and investigative impact, retained in the criminal investigation file.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: By August 1, 2026, and annually thereafter, agencies obtaining warrants for fleeing-vehicle tracking devices must report the number to the BCA superintendent for inclusion in the biennial legislative report.
rule_text_technical: Under § 626A.35, subd. 2c(e), the chief law enforcement officer of an agency obtaining a warrant under (b) must notify the BCA superintendent of the number of search warrants obtained in the preceding 12 months, and the superintendent must summarize this in the bureau's biennial report under § 299C.18.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: Personnel data on certain public officials, including specified executive heads at the Metropolitan Council and chief law enforcement officer of the Metropolitan Transit Police, become public upon completion of an investigation of a complaint or charge unless access would jeopardize an active investigation or reveal confidential sources.
rule_text_technical: Under amended Minn. Stat. § 13.43, subd. 2(e), upon completion of an investigation of a complaint or charge against an enumerated public official (including expanded categories of Metropolitan Council appointees and the Metropolitan Transit Police chief), or upon resignation/termination during pendency, all data relating to the complaint are public, unless access would jeopardize an active investigation or reveal confidential sources.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: An individual who is the subject of body-worn camera (portable recording system) data has a right of access to the recording, and on request must receive a copy with non-consenting subjects' images redacted, except on-duty peace officers' identities generally cannot be redacted.
rule_text_technical: Pursuant to Minn. Stat. § 13.825, subd. 4(a)-(b), portable recording system data subjects (including the collecting peace officer and any individual whose image or voice is documented) have access to the data; copies provided must redact non-consenting subjects, but the identity and activities of an on-duty peace officer engaged in investigation or response may not be redacted unless protected under § 13.82, subd. 17(a).

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: A person entitled to a collision report may obtain unredacted body-worn-camera data from the collision investigation upon written request, but must use the data only for claim processing or related proceedings and may not redisseminate it.
rule_text_technical: Under § 13.825, subd. 4(c), a person entitled to a collision report under § 169.09, subd. 13 must, upon written request accompanied by the accident report, be provided unredacted portable recording system data from the investigation; data may be used only to process a claim or as evidence in proceedings, and may not be further disseminated; violations are subject to remedies and penalties under § 13.08; agencies may deny if disclosure would interfere with active investigation, the data is clearly offensive, or the data is otherwise classified as not public.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: You must not add, share, or disseminate an individual's name, identifying information, or contact information to a patient registry of persons with a specific disability without that individual's informed consent, unless specifically authorized by state or federal law.
rule_text_technical: Under Minn. Stat. § 144.338, subd. 2, except as specifically authorized or required by state or federal law, a person must not add, share, or disseminate to a patient registry an individual's name or other identifying data, or contact information (including home address, telephone number, or electronic mail addresses) without the individual's informed consent. The attorney general may enforce under § 8.31 (excluding § 8.31, subd. 3a remedies); government entities are subject to remedies under §§ 13.08, 13.085, and 13.09.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: The director may share prehospital overdose data—including incident location and time, fatality status, suspected drug type, naloxone administration, and first responder type—with the multi-jurisdiction Overdose Detection Mapping Application Program (ODMAP).
rule_text_technical: Under amended § 144E.123, subd. 3, prehospital care data classified as private under chapter 13 may be shared by the director with the Washington/Baltimore HIDTA's ODMAP, including data identifying location, time, fatality status, suspected drug type, naloxone administration, and first responder type, for purposes including secure user reporting, near real-time mapping, and overdose-related public health/safety resource decisions.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: If a responsible authority notifies a requestor that government data is available for inspection or pickup and the requestor fails to appear within five business days, the entity may suspend further response until the requestor inspects or pays for the copies.
rule_text_technical: Under amended Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(g), if a responsible authority has notified the requesting person that responsive data or copies are available for inspection or collection, and the requestor does not inspect or collect within five business days, the responsible authority may suspend further response until the requestor inspects the data or collects and pays for the copies.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: Educational agencies must treat a parent's home address, telephone number, email, or other personal contact information as private data on individuals and may not designate it as directory information, regardless of any prior designation.
rule_text_technical: Under amended § 13.32, subd. 2(c) and subd. 5(c) and (f), data concerning parents are private data on individuals, and an educational agency or institution may not designate a parent's home address, telephone number, email address, or other personal contact information as directory information; this applies retroactively to previously designated data. Postsecondary institutions are excepted from subd. 5(c). Sharing with the Minnesota Department of Education for federal reporting is required when requested.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: When deciding whether to compel disclosure of not-public government data, the presiding officer must balance the benefit to the requesting party against harm to confidentiality and privacy interests, and may issue protective orders to ensure proper handling.
rule_text_technical: Under amended § 13.03, subd. 6, where a government entity opposes discovery on the grounds that data is classified as not public, the presiding officer must first determine discoverability under applicable rules, and if discoverable, must weigh the benefit to the requesting party against harm to confidentiality interests of the entity, providers, or subjects, and the privacy of identified individuals; the officer must consider whether notice to the data subject is warranted and may issue protective orders, with specific consideration of §§ 611A.90 and 5B.11 for certain protected data.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: The commissioner must collect standardized community supervision data—including sentencing, violations, revocations, early discharges, and restructuring—and analyze the data by race, gender, and county including Tribal Nations.
rule_text_technical: Under amended § 401.17, subd. 5, the advisory committee must establish a method to standardize data classifications across community supervision systems and collect data including the number of individuals sentenced to supervision; offense levels, types, and assessed risk levels; violation/revocation rates and grounds with final dispositions; early discharges; restructurings; and revocations with grounds. Beginning May 1, 2025, the commissioner must analyze the collected data by race, gender, and county, including Tribal Nations.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota House File 2432 — Public Safety — Artificial Intelligence Use

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota HF 2432 — AI in Public Safety (Minnesota, 2025-05-23).

rule_text: The Professional Educator Licensing and Standards Board and the Department of Education must enter into a data sharing agreement to share E-12 educational data and staff automated reporting data for limited purposes of program approval, improvement, and funding management.
rule_text_technical: The Professional Educator Licensing and Standards Board and the Department of Education must enter into a data sharing agreement to share educational data at the E-12 level for the limited purpose of program approval and improvement for teacher education programs, and to share staff automated reporting system data for the limited purpose of managing and processing funding to school districts and other entities.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12 (Minnesota, null).

rule_text: A charter school's management agreement with a CMO or EMO must include policies and protocols meeting federal and state laws on student and personnel data collection, usage, access, retention, disclosure, destruction, and indemnification for data breaches.
rule_text_technical: A management agreement with a CMO or EMO must contain the policies and protocols that meet federal and state laws regarding student and personnel data collection, usage, access, retention, disclosure and destruction, and indemnification and warranty provisions in case of data breaches by the CMO or EMO.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12 (Minnesota, null).

rule_text: The Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact Commission must provide for the exchange of information to administer the compact consistent with generally accepted data protection principles, while preserving each member state's ownership and control over licensee information.
rule_text_technical: The commission shall provide for facilitating the exchange of information to administer and implement the provisions of this compact in accordance with the rules of the commission, consistent with generally accepted data protection principles. Nothing in this compact shall be deemed or construed to alter, limit, or inhibit the power of a member state to control and maintain ownership of its licensee information or alter, limit, or inhibit the laws or regulations governing licensee information in the member state.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12 (Minnesota, null).

rule_text: Member states receiving teacher investigation or disciplinary files from another state must protect the security and confidentiality of those files at least as well as their own and must notify the originating state before any further disclosure.
rule_text_technical: Any member state receiving such information or files shall protect and maintain the security and confidentiality thereof, in at least the same manner that it maintains its own investigatory or disciplinary files and information. Prior to disclosing any disciplinary or investigatory information received from another member state, the disclosing state shall communicate its intention and purpose for such disclosure to the member state which originally provided that information.

first_instance.law_name: Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Minnesota S 3870 — Education Policy for Kindergarten Through Grade 12 (Minnesota, null).

rule_text: The designated education authority must report student literacy assessment performance data in aggregated and disaggregated form, organized by school location and grade level, using specified student demographic categories.

rule_text: You must comply with the Division of Consumer Protection's authority to administer and enforce the Utah Consumer Privacy Act.
rule_text_technical: The Division of Consumer Protection shall administer and enforce Title 13, Chapter 61, Utah Consumer Privacy Act.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: Consumer complaints filed with the Division are protected records and the Division must not publicly disclose the identity of an investigated person unless their identity becomes public in an enforcement proceeding or they consent.
rule_text_technical: A consumer complaint is a protected record under Subsection 63G-2-305(87). In carrying out its duties, the division may not publicly disclose the identity of a person it investigates unless the identity becomes public in an enforcement proceeding or the person consents.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: Before publicly releasing a consumer complaint, the Division must redact the filer's address, social security number, bank account information, email address, telephone number, and similar personal information.
rule_text_technical: Before making a reclassified public consumer complaint or response available to the public, the division shall redact information that would disclose the filer's address, social security number, bank account information, email address, telephone number, or similar information, and may redact the filer's name and other identifying information.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: When disclosing a consumer complaint to a respondent, the Division may redact the filer's bank account information, social security number, identifying information if anonymity is requested, and other information whose disclosure would invade personal privacy.
rule_text_technical: If the division discloses a consumer complaint to the respondent, it may redact the filer's bank account information, social security number, name and identifying information if the filer requests anonymity, and other information the disclosure of which constitutes a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: You must not represent that the Division or state endorses you, omit material facts required in filings, or include false, deceptive, or misleading material statements in filings with the Division.
rule_text_technical: A seller may not represent that the division or state endorses or approves the seller, omit a material statement of fact required by this chapter or rule, or include in a filing a material statement of fact that the seller or principal knew or should have known is false, deceptive, inaccurate, or misleading.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: When providing a credit report to a buyer, you must disclose in writing the credit reporting agency, the name of the credit score model used, and the minimum and maximum possible scores under that model.
rule_text_technical: When a consumer credit services organization provides a credit report to a buyer, the credit services organization shall provide a written disclosure identifying the credit reporting agency, the name of the credit score model used to calculate the credit score, and the minimum and maximum possible scores under the credit score model.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: Definition: a 'credit score' is a numerical value or categorization derived from information in a consumer report and from a statistical tool or modeling system, developed to predict the likelihood of credit behavior, including risk predictors and risk scores.
rule_text_technical: 'Credit score' means a numerical value or categorization that a person derives from information in a consumer report, derives from a statistical tool or modeling system, and develops to predict the likelihood of credit behavior, including a risk predictor or risk score.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: The Division must operate a system to receive consumer reports about financial institutions' or companies' use or creation of social credit scores and submit an annual report to the Legislature summarizing reports indicating use of social credit scores for discriminatory or preferential treatment.
rule_text_technical: The division shall establish and operate a system to receive consumer reports regarding a financial institution's or company's use or creation of a social credit score, and before November 1 of each year submit a written report to the Business and Labor Interim Committee summarizing the reports received indicating use of social credit scores to discriminate against, advocate for, or cause adverse or preferential treatment of a person.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

rule_text: If you operate a mental health chatbot using generative AI that simulates therapist-like confidential communications or that a reasonable person would believe provides mental health therapy, you are subject to this chapter's requirements.
rule_text_technical: A 'mental health chatbot' is defined as generative AI technology engaging in interactive conversations similar to confidential communications with a licensed mental health therapist, where a supplier represents or a reasonable person would believe it provides mental health therapy, excluding scripted outputs and AI that only connects users to human therapists.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you operate an app store, you must collect and share age category data with developers about whether a user is a child, younger teenager, older teenager, or adult.
rule_text_technical: 'Age category data' means information about a user's age category collected by an app store provider and shared with a developer, with categories of child (under 13), younger teenager (13-15), older teenager (16-17), and adult (18+).

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you operate an app store, before obtaining parental consent you must clearly disclose the app's age rating, content description, what personal data the app collects from users and shares with third parties, and how the developer protects that data.
rule_text_technical: Parental consent disclosure must include the app's age rating and content description (if available), description of personal data collected from a user and shared with third parties, and the methods implemented by the developer to protect personal data.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you provide earned wage access services, before entering an agreement with a consumer you must clearly and conspicuously disclose the consumer's rights, all fees, and any voluntary tip, gratuity, or donation opportunities.
rule_text_technical: A provider shall, before entering into an agreement for earned wage access services with a consumer, clearly and conspicuously disclose the consumer's rights under the agreement, all fees, and any voluntary tip, gratuity, or donation opportunities.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you provide earned wage access services, you must comply with all applicable local, state, and federal privacy and information security laws.
rule_text_technical: A provider shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal privacy and information security laws.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you provide earned wage access services, you may not use a consumer's credit report or credit score to determine eligibility for the services.
rule_text_technical: A provider may not use a consumer's credit report or credit score as defined by 15 U.S.C. Sec. 1681 et seq. to determine eligibility for earned wage access services.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you process specific geolocation data—information that directly identifies an individual's specific location accurate within 1,750 feet or less—it qualifies as sensitive data subject to heightened protections.
rule_text_technical: 'Specific geolocation data' means information derived from technology, including GPS-level latitude and longitude, that directly identifies an individual's specific location, accurate within a radius of 1,750 feet or less; excludes content of communications and data generated by/connected to advanced utility metering infrastructure.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you engage in targeted advertising—displaying ads selected based on personal data from a consumer's activities over time across nonaffiliated websites or applications to predict preferences—you must comply with consumer rights and disclosure requirements.
rule_text_technical: 'Targeted advertising' means displaying advertisements selected based on personal data obtained from a consumer's activities over time and across nonaffiliated websites or online applications to predict preferences or interests; excludes advertising within a controller's affiliated properties, contextual advertising, response to direct requests, and processing solely for measurement/reporting of performance, reach, or frequency.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you sell personal data—exchanging it for monetary consideration to a third party—you must comply with consumer rights and disclosure obligations under this chapter.
rule_text_technical: 'Sale,' 'sell,' or 'sold' means the exchange of personal data for monetary consideration by a controller to a third party; excludes disclosures to processors, affiliates, third parties consistent with consumer's reasonable expectations, consumer-directed transfers, consumer disclosures for requested products/services, public disclosures, and merger/acquisition/bankruptcy transfers.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: If you process pseudonymous data, you must keep the additional information needed to attribute it to a specific individual separate and subject to appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure data is not attributable to an identified individual.
rule_text_technical: 'Pseudonymous data' means personal data that cannot be attributed to a specific individual without the use of additional information, if the additional information is kept separate from the consumer's personal data and subject to appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure the personal data are not attributable to an identified or identifiable individual.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications (Utah, 2026-03-17).

rule_text: When making material modifications to an app's terms or privacy policy that change data collection categories, age ratings, monetization, or functionality, these must be treated as 'significant changes' triggering disclosure requirements.
rule_text_technical: A 'significant change' is defined as a material modification to an app's terms of service or privacy policy that changes categories of data collected/stored/shared, alters age rating or content descriptions, adds new monetization features (in-app purchases, advertisements), or materially changes functionality or user experience.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

rule_text: Audio or video recordings created by body-worn cameras inside hospitals, healthcare facilities, clinics, or human services programs must be classified as protected records, except in specified circumstances such as recording crimes or officer-involved incidents.
rule_text_technical: Body-worn camera recordings that record sound or images inside a hospital, health care facility, clinic, or human service program are protected records, except recordings that depict commission of an alleged crime, record encounters resulting in death/bodily injury or weapon discharge, are subject of complaint or legal proceeding, contain officer-involved critical incidents, or have been requested for reclassification by a featured subject.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

rule_text_technical: An image taken of an individual during the process of booking the individual into jail is a protected record, unless the individual is convicted of the related criminal offense, a law enforcement agency releases the image due to fugitive/threat status or to potential witnesses with direct knowledge, a judge orders release for a legitimate law enforcement interest, or the image is displayed to a person permitted under Section 17-72-802.

first_instance.law_name: Utah S 38 — Consumer Protection Modifications

rule_text: You are not criminally or civilly liable for handling obscene CSAM when acting in good faith as a covered entity, law enforcement, court personnel, juror, attorney, DHHS or CJC employee within scope of authorized duties.
rule_text_technical: Immunity from criminal/civil liability under Section 76-5b-209 for entities and specified personnel acting in good faith compliance with Section 77-4-201 in performing reporting, data preservation, detection/prevention policies, or authorized law enforcement, judicial, or agency duties.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

rule_text: You must understand that, unless an offense specifically requires it, prurient-interest appeal and patently-offensive portrayal are not elements of offenses in the Sexual Exploitation Act.
rule_text_technical: Unless specifically provided in the offense, it is not an element of an offense in Chapter 5b that the material appeal to the prurient interest in sex of the average person nor that prohibited conduct be portrayed in a patently offensive manner.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

rule_text: You may, as a library administrator, disable the content-filtering technology protection measure at the request of an adult library patron and to enable access for research or other lawful purposes.
rule_text_technical: An administrator, supervisor, or representative of a public library may disable the technology protection measure at the request of an adult library patron and to enable access for research or other lawful purposes.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must, as defense counsel leaving discovery materials with a jailed prisoner, ensure those materials contain no CSAM, apparent CSAM, obscene CSAM, intimate images, personal identifying information of others, or financial information of others.
rule_text_technical: Counsel leaving discovery, evidence, or documents with a prisoner at jail must ensure they do not include visual depictions of individuals under 18, personal identifying information of others, financial information of others, CSAM, apparent CSAM, obscene CSAM, intimate images, or any visual depiction prohibited by jail policy.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: Data protection authorities and sector-specific health regulators must not retain child sexual abuse material or content appearing to depict child sexual abuse longer than necessary to meet legal requirements for reporting and evidence preservation.
rule_text_technical: The department or a division within the department may not retain CSAM, apparent CSAM, or obscene CSAM longer than necessary to comply with the requirements of Section 26B-1-234.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must, when CSAM, apparent CSAM, or obscene CSAM is obtained because an employee unlawfully viewed it, consult Human Resource Management on personnel action and local law enforcement on retention.
rule_text_technical: Where the department or division obtains CSAM, apparent CSAM, or obscene CSAM as a result of an employee unlawfully viewing such material, the department or division shall consult and follow guidance of the Division of Human Resource Management regarding personnel action and local law enforcement regarding retention.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must, when the department obtains CSAM, apparent CSAM, or obscene CSAM through reports or investigations, immediately secure the material or device and contact the law enforcement agency with jurisdiction.
rule_text_technical: When the department or division obtains CSAM, apparent CSAM, or obscene CSAM as a result of a report or investigation, it shall immediately secure the material or the electronic device (if digital) and contact the law enforcement office with jurisdiction over the area where the case is located.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

rule_text: You must, as the Office of Background Processing, adopt measures to strictly limit access to applicants' personal identifying information to those individuals responsible for processing background-check applications and protect that information's security.
rule_text_technical: The office shall adopt measures to strictly limit access to personal identifying information solely to individuals responsible for processing and entering background-check applications, and to protect the security of personal identifying information reviewed under Subsection (3).

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must, as a background-check applicant, provide signed consent for initial and ongoing background checks, fingerprint-based monitoring, and retention of personal identifying information including fingerprints.
rule_text_technical: Applicants must submit a disclosure form for consent to initial background check, ongoing fingerprint and registry monitoring until 180 days after disassociation, additional checks where reasonable cause exists, and retention of personal identifying information including fingerprints for monitoring and notification.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must, as the bureau, discard and destroy retained fingerprints and notify the FBI to do the same once an individual's direct-access qualified status ends.
rule_text_technical: Upon notice that an individual with direct access qualified status will no longer be associated with a certification, contract, or licensee, the bureau shall discard and destroy retained fingerprints and notify the FBI to discard and destroy the retained fingerprints from the NGI System.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: You must understand that apparent CSAM, CSAM, and obscene CSAM are excluded from the definition of 'record' under Utah's records access law and are not subject to public records disclosure.
rule_text_technical: The definition of 'record' under GRAMA excludes apparent child sexual abuse material, child sexual abuse material, and obscene child sexual abuse material as defined in Section 76-5b-103.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: Internet service providers, electronic communications services, telecommunications providers, and cable operators are exempt from computer-technician reporting requirements if they comply with federal child sexual abuse material reporting obligations.
rule_text_technical: Section 76-5b-206 does not apply to internet service providers, interactive computer services (47 U.S.C. § 230(f)(2)), electronic communications service providers (18 U.S.C. § 2510), telecommunications/information/mobile services (47 U.S.C. § 153), or cable operators (47 U.S.C. § 522), if the provider reports the image in compliance with 18 U.S.C. § 2258A or successor federal CSAM-reporting statute.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: A court must not grant custody of a minor child to a non-parent who has been convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or pleaded no contest to a felony involving possession or distribution of apparent child sexual abuse material, or unlawful activity regarding obscene material depicting the sexual abuse of a minor, except as permitted under the rehabilitation exception.
rule_text_technical: A court may not grant custody under Section 81-9-402 to a non-parent who, before a custody order is issued, is convicted, pleads guilty, or pleads no contest to a felony or attempted felony involving conduct constituting possession of apparent child sexual abuse material (76-5b-207), distribution of apparent child sexual abuse material (76-5b-208), or unlawful activity regarding obscene material depicting the sexual abuse of a minor (76-5b-209), unless Subsection (11) criteria are met.

first_instance.law_name: Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Utah H 289 — Child Sexual Abuse Material Amendments (Utah, 2026-03-24).

rule_text: An adult must not adopt a minor child if, before adoption is finalized, they have been convicted of a felony involving possession or distribution of apparent child sexual abuse material, or unlawful activity regarding obscene material depicting the sexual abuse of a minor, unless the rehabilitation exception applies.
rule_text_technical: An adult may not adopt a minor child if, before adoption is finalized, the adult has been convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or pleaded no contest to a felony or attempted felony involving conduct constituting possession of apparent child sexual abuse material (76-5b-207), distribution of apparent child sexual abuse material (76-5b-208), or unlawful activity regarding obscene material depicting the sexual abuse of a minor (76-5b-209), except as provided in Subsection (7).

rule_text: The government must promote knowledge and reduce vulnerabilities with respect to AI to strengthen digital trust and security, including measures against cybersecurity risks in AI systems.
rule_text_technical: Promover el conocimiento y disminuir las vulnerabilidades con respecto a la IA para fortalecer la confianza y la seguridad digital, incluyendo medidas contra riesgos de ciberseguridad en sistemas de IA.

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Colombia CONPES 4144 — National AI Policy (Colombia, 2025-02-14).

rule_text: AI development must follow the Unesco Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, ensuring equitable access to AI advances, knowledge sharing, and protection of human dignity, well-being and prevention of harm.
rule_text_technical: El desarrollo de la IA debe seguir la Recomendación sobre la Ética de la IA de la Unesco, asegurando acceso equitativo a los avances en IA, intercambio de conocimientos y protección de la dignidad humana, bienestar y prevención de daños.

rule_text: MinCiencias, with MinTIC, DAPRE, DNP and CRC, must issue in 2025 a 'Strategy of recommendations for the ethical development, implementation and use of AI' addressed to private sector organizations, academia, and private research ecosystems that develop, implement, or use AI systems.
rule_text_technical: Estrategia de recomendaciones para desarrollo, implementación y uso ético de IA dirigida a organizaciones del sector privado, academia y ecosistemas de investigación privados.

rule_text: DAPRE, with MinCIT, MinTIC, SIC and DNP, must design and implement between 2025 and 2026 a collaborative data space (data trust) to drive personal data portability and mobility, providing technological infrastructure, data governance model, and user applications.
rule_text_technical: Diseño e implementación de espacio colaborativo de datos (data trust) para portabilidad y movilidad de datos personales con infraestructura tecnológica, gobierno de datos y aplicaciones al usuario.

rule_text: The Ministry of Education, with MinCiencias, must implement strategies that integrate the pedagogical, ethical, responsible, and sustainable use of AI and strengthen the digital competencies of students and teachers between 2025 and 2030.
rule_text_technical: Implementación de estrategias que integren el uso pedagógico, ético, responsable y sostenible de la IA y fortalecimiento de competencias digitales de estudiantes y docentes.

rule_text_technical: Estrategia de sensibilización para que IES incluyan componente de formación ética en programas relacionados con sistemas de IA, incentivando reconocimiento, monitoreo, control, mitigación y prevención de efectos adversos.

rule_text: MinTIC must update and disseminate during 2025 the Information Security and Privacy Model as part of the Digital Government Policy as a transversal model integrating challenges related to trust and digital security of AI systems, including effective identification, management, treatment, and mitigation of digital risks and threats associated with AI.
rule_text_technical: Actualización del Modelo de Seguridad y Privacidad de la información integrando desafíos de confianza y seguridad digital de sistemas de IA, con identificación, gestión, tratamiento y mitigación de riesgos y amenazas digitales asociados a la IA.

rule_text_technical: Estrategia para incorporación y uso ético, crítico, responsable y sostenible de la IA en sector audiovisual, cinematográfico, sonoro, medios interactivos y comunicación, abordando riesgos en derechos culturales, PI, sesgos algorítmicos, inclusión y accesibilidad.

rule_text: You should apply training data sanitization (such as activation clustering or latent feature outlier detection) to detect backdoor poisoning samples in training datasets.
rule_text_technical: Backdoor mitigation should include sanitization techniques such as outlier detection in latent feature space and activation clustering to isolate backdoored training samples.

first_instance.law_name: NIST AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning — A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025 Edition)

rule_text: You should apply Byzantine-resilient aggregation rules in federated learning to identify and exclude malicious client updates that could poison the global model.
rule_text_technical: Federated learning systems should implement Byzantine-resilient aggregation rules to detect and exclude malicious local model updates from compromised clients.

first_instance.law_name: NIST AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning — A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025 Edition)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIST AI 100-2 E2025 — Adversarial Machine Learning (United States, 2025-03-24).

rule_text: You should evaluate GenAI agents specifically for vulnerabilities arising from their tool use and iterative prompting and implement controls to manage agent-specific security risks.
rule_text_technical: Developers and deployers of LLM-based agents should conduct agent-specific vulnerability assessments and implement interventions to manage risks from arbitrary code execution, data exfiltration, and tool misuse stemming from prompt injection.

first_instance.law_name: NIST AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning — A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025 Edition)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIST AI 100-2 E2025 — Adversarial Machine Learning (United States, 2025-03-24).

rule_text: You should manage AI supply-chain risks by addressing the potential for undetectable Trojans and intentional exploits planted in models, including preventing insider threats throughout the supply chain.
rule_text_technical: Organizations should implement supply-chain risk management practices addressing the potential for undetectable backdoors and Trojans in AI models, including insider threat controls across model development pipelines.

first_instance.law_name: NIST AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning — A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025 Edition)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIST AI 100-2 E2025 — Adversarial Machine Learning (United States, 2025-03-24).

rule_text: You should continuously monitor the behavior of deployed quantized models because quantization can introduce additional vulnerabilities and may be exploited to produce harmful quantized variants from benign full-precision models.
rule_text_technical: Organizations deploying quantized AI models should perform continuous behavioral monitoring, recognizing that quantization may amplify adversarial vulnerabilities and may be exploited to produce malicious quantized models from benign full-precision counterparts.

rule_text: You should ensure harms caused through AI systems are investigated and redressed by enacting strong enforcement and remedial mechanisms (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States should ensure that harms caused through AI systems are investigated and redressed by enacting strong enforcement mechanisms and remedial actions, including remediation mechanisms provided by private and public sector companies, promoting auditability and traceability.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should consider adding the role of an independent AI Ethics Officer or similar mechanism to oversee impact assessment, auditing and continuous monitoring (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States should encourage public entities, private sector companies and civil society organizations to involve different stakeholders in their AI governance and to consider adding the role of an independent AI Ethics Officer or some other mechanism to oversee ethical impact assessment, auditing and continuous monitoring, and to create a network of such officers.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should ensure that AI systems used by the judiciary include sufficient safeguards to protect fundamental rights, judicial independence, and the principle of human oversight (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States should enhance judicial capacity to make decisions on AI systems and, when AI systems are used by the judiciary, ensure sufficient safeguards to guarantee protection of fundamental human rights, the rule of law, judicial independence and human oversight, ensuring trustworthy, public-interest oriented and human-centric use.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should subject AI systems used in learning to strict requirements for monitoring, ability assessment, or behaviour prediction, and prohibit misuse of learner data including for commercial purposes (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: AI systems used in learning should be subject to strict requirements for monitoring, assessment of abilities, or prediction of learner behaviours, supporting learning without reducing cognitive abilities or extracting sensitive information, in compliance with personal data protection standards; data collected during learner interactions must not be subject to misuse, misappropriation or criminal exploitation, including commercial purposes.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should take steps to ensure competitive markets, prevent abuse of dominant positions in AI markets, and respect ethical standards when exporting AI products to jurisdictions lacking such standards (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States should take appropriate steps to ensure competitive markets and consumer protection, prevent abuse of dominant market positions including monopolies in relation to AI systems throughout their life cycle, and AI actors developing AI in countries with established ethical standards should respect those standards when exporting, developing or applying AI in countries lacking such standards.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should regulate AI prediction, detection and treatment solutions in healthcare with bias oversight, domain-expert inclusion, privacy compliance, informed consent, human final diagnosis, and ethical research review (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States should pay particular attention in regulating prediction, detection and treatment AI solutions in health care by: ensuring oversight to minimize bias; including the professional, patient or service user as 'domain expert' in algorithm development; ensuring privacy and meeting data protection requirements; ensuring informed consent for use and analysis of personal data without preventing access to care; ensuring final diagnosis and treatment decisions are taken by humans; and ensuring ethical research committee review prior to clinical use where necessary.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: You should put in place mechanisms to meaningfully engage children and young people in decisions about how AI systems impact their lives (recommendation).
rule_text_technical: Member States and all stakeholders should put in place mechanisms to meaningfully engage children and young people in conversations, debates and decision-making with regard to the impact of AI systems on their lives and futures.

first_instance.law_name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (UNESCO, 2021-11-23).

rule_text: If you develop or provide AI-based products or services or otherwise utilize AI in business, you must endeavor to improve efficiency and create new industries through proactive use of AI and cooperate with national and local government measures.

rule_text: Your declaration, opinion request or authorization request must specify the controller's identity, processing purposes, interconnections, data categories, retention period, services involved, recipients, access rights, security measures, use of subprocessors, and any cross-border transfers.

rule_text: You must keep personal data accurate and up to date, and take all reasonable steps to erase or rectify inaccurate or incomplete data.
rule_text_technical: Collected data must be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date; all reasonable measures must be taken to ensure that inaccurate or incomplete data, in light of the purposes for which they are collected and further processed, are erased or rectified.

rule_text: You may process health data only with the subject's consent or where necessary for vital interests, legal purposes, public health, prevention of danger or offences, legal claims, or medical care under professional secrecy.

rule_text: You must collect health data directly from the data subject, except where collection from other sources is necessary for the processing or where the subject cannot provide them.

rule_text: You may only interconnect files to achieve legitimate legal or statutory objectives, without causing discrimination or reducing rights, and with appropriate security measures and respect for relevance of data.
