rule_text: When handling sensitive personal information, you must additionally notify individuals of the necessity of the handling and its influence on their rights and interests.
rule_text_technical: Personal information handlers handling sensitive personal information shall, in addition to items in Article 17(1), notify individuals of the necessity and influence on the individual's rights and interests, except where the Law permits no notification.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

rule_text: State organs handling personal information to fulfill statutory duties must act according to the powers and procedures provided by law and may not exceed the scope or extent necessary to fulfill those duties.
rule_text_technical: State organs handling personal information to fulfill statutory duties shall conduct them according to the powers and procedures provided in laws or administrative regulations and may not exceed the scope or extent necessary to fulfill statutory duties.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

rule_text: Before transferring personal information outside China, you must notify the individual of the foreign recipient's name, contact, purpose, methods, data categories, and rights-exercise procedures, and obtain the individual's separate consent.
rule_text_technical: Where personal information handlers provide personal information outside the PRC, they shall notify the individual of the foreign receiving side's name, contact method, purpose, methods, categories, and ways/procedures to exercise rights with the foreign receiver, and obtain separate consent.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

Both rules require informing the data subject of risks before cross-border transfer based on consent, but the Saudi rule uses explicit consent as the transfer mechanism itself, while China's PIPL rule focuses on notification of recipient details and requires separate legal mechanisms beyond consent alone.

rule_text: You cannot provide personal information stored in mainland China to foreign judicial or law enforcement authorities without approval from the competent PRC authorities.
rule_text_technical: Without the approval of the competent authorities of the PRC, personal information handlers may not provide personal information stored within the mainland territory of the PRC to foreign judicial or law enforcement agencies.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

rule_text: You must regularly audit your personal information handling activities for compliance with laws and administrative regulations.
rule_text_technical: Personal information handlers shall regularly engage in audits of their personal information handling and compliance with laws and administrative regulations.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

Both require auditing of personal data processing for compliance, but Oman's rule is triggered by a Ministry request and mandates an external auditor with a copy of the report provided to the Ministry, whereas China's PIPL requires the controller to regularly self-audit without an external auditor or government-triggered mechanism.
Both independently require regular audits of personal data handling/protection compliance, though drafted in different regulatory contexts and with different phrasing.

Both require periodic audits of data/algorithmic processing for compliance, but the Mexican rule focuses specifically on discriminatory impacts of algorithmic systems and mandates corrective action, while the Chinese rule covers general compliance with laws and regulations for personal information handling.

rule_text: If you provide important Internet platform services with large user numbers and complex business models, you must establish compliance systems and an independent oversight body of mainly external members, formulate fair platform rules clarifying internal providers' duties, cease serving on-platform providers that seriously violate the law, and publish regular personal information protection social responsibility reports.
rule_text_technical: Personal information handlers providing important Internet platform services, with large user numbers and complex business models, shall: establish personal information protection compliance systems with an independent body composed mainly of outside members; formulate platform rules under principles of openness, fairness, and justice clarifying intra-platform providers' handling standards and duties; stop serving on-platform providers that seriously violate the law in handling personal information; and regularly release personal information protection social responsibility reports.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions

instances.notes: Rule introduced in China PIPL (AI provisions) (China, 2021-08-20).

rule_text: You must notify the Commission d'accès à l'information in writing of the title, contact information and starting date of the person in charge of the protection of personal information.
rule_text_technical: A public body must, as soon as possible, notify the Commission in writing of the title, contact information and starting date of the person who exercises the function of person in charge of the protection of personal information.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

Both require notifying the supervisory authority of the appointment of a data protection/privacy officer, though Zimbabwe's rule is framed as a general duty to 'duly notify' while Quebec's rule specifies written notification with contact details and start date.

Both require notification of a data protection officer's contact details to the supervisory authority, but the Sri Lanka rule also requires public publication of those details, whereas the Quebec rule focuses on notifying the Commission of the person in charge's title and contact information only.

Both require notifying a data protection authority of a designated officer's appointment, but Malaysia's rule covers a data protection officer generally while Quebec's rule specifically covers the person in charge of personal information protection with title and contact details.

rule_text: You may rely on consent only for the time necessary to achieve the purposes for which it was requested.
rule_text_technical: Consent is valid only for the time necessary to achieve the purposes for which it was requested.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

Both rules restrict data use to the declared purposes for which consent/collection occurred, but the DGA rule specifically targets Recognised Data Altruism Organisations and general-interest purposes, whereas the Quebec rule concerns time-limited consent for any personal data processing.
Both address temporal specificity of consent, but Jordan additionally requires specificity of purpose, whereas Québec's rule focuses solely on limiting consent to the time necessary.

rule_text: Personal information is sensitive if, due to its nature (medical, biometric, intimate) or context, it entails a high level of reasonable expectation of privacy.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of the Act, personal information is sensitive if, due to its nature, in particular its medical, biometric or otherwise intimate nature, or the context of its use or release, it entails a high level of reasonable expectation of privacy.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must publish governance rules regarding personal information on your public body's website, approved by your access/privacy committee.
rule_text_technical: A public body must publish on its website governance rules regarding personal information, approved by its committee on access to information and the protection of personal information; the rules must define roles and responsibilities throughout the life cycle of information, provide a complaints process, and describe training and awareness activities.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must ensure that privacy settings on technological products or services offered to the public provide the highest level of confidentiality by default, without intervention by the person concerned.
rule_text_technical: A public body that collects personal information when offering to the public a technological product or service having privacy settings must ensure that those settings provide the highest level of confidentiality by default, without any intervention by the person concerned; this does not apply to browser cookie settings.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must take reasonable measures to reduce the risk of injury and prevent recurrence when you have cause to believe a confidentiality incident has occurred, and notify the Commission and affected persons promptly if it presents a risk of serious injury.
rule_text_technical: A public body that has cause to believe a confidentiality incident involving personal information it holds has occurred must take reasonable measures to reduce the risk of injury and prevent new incidents; if the incident presents a risk of serious injury, the body must promptly notify the Commission and any affected person, failing which the Commission may order it to do so.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

Both require reporting privacy breaches to a government authority, but Ontario Bill 194 amends FIPPA to cover a broad range of unauthorized data handling acts by Ontario public sector institutions, whereas Quebec's Law 25 focuses on confidentiality incidents and risk-reduction measures with reporting to the Commission d'accès à l'information.

rule_text: A 'confidentiality incident' means unauthorized access, use or release of personal information, or loss or other breach of protection of such information.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of the Act, 'confidentiality incident' means access, use or release not authorized by law of personal information, or loss of personal information or any other breach of the protection of such information.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must consider the sensitivity of the information, anticipated consequences, and likelihood of injurious use when assessing risk of injury from a confidentiality incident, and consult your privacy officer.
rule_text_technical: In assessing the risk of injury to a person whose personal information is concerned by a confidentiality incident, a public body must consider the sensitivity of the information, anticipated consequences of its use, and the likelihood that such information will be used for injurious purposes, and must consult the person in charge of the protection of personal information.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must inform individuals of the use of identification, location, or profiling technology and the means available to activate those functions before collecting their personal information.
rule_text_technical: Anyone who collects personal information from the person concerned using technology that includes functions allowing the person to be identified, located or profiled must first inform the person of the use of such technology and of the means available to activate those functions.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must take reasonable measures to limit the risk of someone identifying a natural person when using de-identified information.
rule_text_technical: A public body that uses de-identified information must take reasonable measures to limit the risk of someone identifying a natural person using de-identified information.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may release personal information without consent to a person or body for study, research, or statistical purposes only after a privacy impact assessment confirms specific necessity criteria are met.
rule_text_technical: A public body may release personal information without consent for study or research purposes or for the production of statistics if a PIA concludes that the objective can be achieved only with identifiable information, obtaining consent is unreasonable, the public interest outweighs the privacy impact, confidentiality is ensured, and only necessary information is released.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must enter into a written agreement before releasing personal information for research/statistical purposes containing specified confidentiality, use limitation, preservation, and notification clauses.
rule_text_technical: A public body that releases personal information under section 67.2.1 must first enter into an agreement with the recipient stipulating restricted access, prohibition on non-research uses, prohibition on unauthorized matching, prohibition on identifiable distribution, protection measures, preservation period, destruction notification, and incident reporting; the agreement must be sent to the Commission and comes into force 30 days after receipt.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must conduct a privacy impact assessment before releasing personal information outside Québec, considering sensitivity, purposes, protection measures, and the legal framework in the receiving State.
rule_text_technical: Before releasing personal information outside Québec, a public body must conduct a PIA taking into account the sensitivity, purposes, contractual and other protection measures, and applicable legal framework in the receiving State; the information may be released only if the assessment establishes adequate protection, and the release must be subject to a written agreement.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: Information is anonymized only if it is reasonably foreseeable at all times that it irreversibly no longer allows direct or indirect identification.
rule_text_technical: For the purposes of the Act, information concerning a natural person is anonymized if it is, at all times, reasonably foreseeable in the circumstances that it irreversibly no longer allows the person to be identified directly or indirectly.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may release personal information about a deceased person to the spouse or close relative if it could help with grieving and the deceased did not record refusal in writing.
rule_text_technical: A public body may release personal information concerning a deceased person to the spouse or a close relative if knowledge of the information could help the applicant in the grieving process and the deceased person did not record in writing his refusal to grant such a right of access.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must comply with formal demands from the Commission to file information or documents to verify compliance with the Act, regardless of prior submissions.
rule_text_technical: The Commission may, by formal demand notified by any appropriate method, require any person, whether subject to the Act or not, to file information or documents to verify compliance; the recipient must comply within the specified time regardless of prior filings.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

rule_text: The Commission may order any person to take measures to protect the rights of persons concerned by a confidentiality incident, including return or destruction of the personal information involved.
rule_text_technical: The Commission may, when a confidentiality incident is brought to its attention, order any person, after giving him the opportunity to submit observations, to take any measure to protect the rights of the persons concerned, including ordering that the personal information involved be returned to the public body or destroyed.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You commit an offence punishable by fines of $1,000-$10,000 (natural persons) or $3,000-$30,000 (others) for acts such as denying access, unlawful collection or destruction, or failing to report confidentiality incidents.
rule_text_technical: Anyone who denies/impedes access, grants unauthorized access, hinders the privacy officer, collects/uses/keeps/destroys personal information in contravention of the law, fails to report a confidentiality incident, or fails to comply with section 67.2.3 conditions commits an offence and is liable to a fine of $1,000 to $10,000 (natural person) or $3,000 to $30,000 (others).

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You commit an offence punishable by fines up to $100,000 (natural persons) or $150,000 (others) for unlawful release, attempted re-identification, obstructing inquiries, ignoring Commission demands or orders, or failing to take security measures.
rule_text_technical: Anyone who releases personal information unlawfully, identifies or attempts to identify a natural person using de-identified or anonymized information without authorization, impedes a Commission inquiry, refuses to comply with a section 127.1 demand, fails to comply with a Commission order, or fails to take security measures under section 63.1 commits an offence with fines of $5,000 to $100,000 (natural person) or $15,000 to $150,000 (others).

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: Individuals are entitled to punitive damages of not less than $1,000 where the unlawful infringement of a right is intentional or results from gross fault.
rule_text_technical: Where the unlawful infringement of a right recognized by Chapter III causes injury and the infringement is intentional or results from a gross fault, the court shall award punitive damages of not less than $1,000.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may collect and use personal information of electors only for election, political financing, or political activity purposes, and only with consent of the person concerned.
rule_text_technical: A political party, independent Member or independent candidate may collect only personal information of electors necessary for election, political financing or political activity purposes, may use it only for those same purposes, and may not collect or use such information without the consent of the person concerned.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must keep a register of confidentiality incidents and send a copy to the Commission upon request.
rule_text_technical: A person carrying on an enterprise must keep a register of confidentiality incidents; a copy must be sent to the Commission at its request.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must inform individuals of the use of identification, location, or profiling technology and means to activate those functions before collecting their personal information.
rule_text_technical: Any person who collects personal information using technology with functions allowing the person to be identified, located or profiled must first inform the person of the use of such technology and the means available to activate those functions.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must publish a confidentiality policy in clear and simple language on your website if you collect personal information through technological means.
rule_text_technical: Any person who collects personal information through technological means must publish on the enterprise's website a confidentiality policy drafted in clear and simple language and disseminate it by any appropriate means; the same applies to amendment notices.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must ensure that privacy settings on technological products or services offered to the public provide the highest level of confidentiality by default.
rule_text_technical: Any person carrying on an enterprise who collects personal information when offering to the public a technological product or service having privacy settings must ensure those settings provide the highest level of confidentiality by default, without intervention by the person concerned; this does not apply to browser cookie settings.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).
Both require privacy-by-design and data minimization by default from the design stage of systems, independently enacted in different jurisdictions.

rule_text: You must keep personal information used to make a decision concerning the person for at least one year following the decision.
rule_text_technical: The information used to make a decision concerning a person is kept for at least one year following the decision.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may communicate personal information without consent to a mandatary or contractor only via written mandate/contract specifying confidentiality, use limitations, and post-mandate destruction obligations.
rule_text_technical: A person carrying on an enterprise may communicate personal information without consent to any person or body for carrying out a mandate or contract entrusted to them, provided the mandate is in writing and specifies confidentiality measures, use limitations, and prohibition on retention beyond the mandate; the mandatary must notify violations to the privacy officer and allow verification.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may communicate personal information to a counterparty for a commercial transaction without consent only under a prior written agreement restricting use, prohibiting unauthorized disclosure, requiring protection, and requiring destruction if the transaction does not close.
rule_text_technical: Where communication is necessary for concluding a commercial transaction, the person carrying on an enterprise may communicate personal information without consent to the other party only after entering an agreement under which the other party undertakes to use it only for concluding the transaction, not communicate without consent, take protection measures, and destroy if the transaction is not concluded; if concluded, the recipient must notify the person concerned within a reasonable time.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must enter into a written agreement before communicating personal information for research/statistical purposes containing specified confidentiality, use limitation, and notification clauses, and send it to the Commission.
rule_text_technical: A person communicating personal information under section 21 must enter into a written agreement with the recipient stipulating restricted access, use limitations, no unauthorized matching, no identifiable distribution, protection measures, preservation period, destruction notification, and incident reporting; the agreement must be sent to the Commission and comes into force 30 days after receipt.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must identify yourself and inform individuals of their right to withdraw consent when using their personal information for commercial or philanthropic prospection, and cease use upon withdrawal.
rule_text_technical: Any person using personal information for commercial or philanthropic prospection purposes must identify himself to the person addressed and inform that person of his right to withdraw his consent to use of personal information for such purposes; upon withdrawal, the information must cease to be used for those purposes.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: Individuals have the right to require an enterprise to cease disseminating personal information or de-index/re-index hyperlinks where dissemination contravenes law or causes serious injury that outweighs public interest.
rule_text_technical: The person to whom personal information relates may require any person carrying on an enterprise to cease dissemination or de-index/re-index hyperlinks attached to his name where dissemination contravenes the law or court order, or where dissemination causes serious injury to reputation/privacy that clearly outweighs public interest in knowing the information or freedom of expression, and the requested action does not exceed what is necessary to prevent perpetuation of the injury.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You may not take or threaten reprisal against a person for filing a complaint with the Commission in good faith or cooperating in an investigation.
rule_text_technical: It is forbidden to take a reprisal against a person on the ground that the person has, in good faith, filed a complaint with the Commission or cooperated in an investigation; threats of reprisal to dissuade from filing or cooperating are also forbidden.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must comply with formal demands from the Commission for information or documents to verify compliance with the Act.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: The Commission may order any person to take measures to protect rights of persons concerned by a confidentiality incident, including return or destruction of the information.
rule_text_technical: The Commission may, when a confidentiality incident is brought to its attention, order any person, after giving an opportunity to submit observations, to take any measure to protect the rights of the persons concerned, including ordering return or destruction of the personal information.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: A monetary administrative penalty may be imposed for failures including improper consent notice, unlawful collection/use/communication, failure to report incidents, lack of security measures, or breach of automated decision rules.
rule_text_technical: A monetary administrative penalty may be imposed by a designated person on anyone who: fails to inform persons concerned per ss. 7-8; collects, uses, communicates, keeps or destroys personal information unlawfully; fails to report a confidentiality incident; fails to take security measures per s. 10; fails to inform of automated decisions or give opportunity to submit observations contrary to s. 12.1; or being a personal information agent contravenes specified sections.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: Maximum monetary administrative penalties are $50,000 for natural persons or, in all other cases, the greater of $10,000,000 or 2% of worldwide turnover for the preceding fiscal year.
rule_text_technical: The maximum amount of the monetary administrative penalty is $50,000 in the case of a natural person and, in all other cases, $10,000,000 or, if greater, the amount corresponding to 2% of worldwide turnover for the preceding fiscal year.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You commit an offence punishable by fines up to $100,000 (natural persons) or the greater of $25,000,000 or 4% of worldwide turnover (others) for unlawful collection/use/communication, failure to report incidents, attempted re-identification, or failure to comply with Commission orders.
rule_text_technical: Anyone who collects, uses, communicates, keeps or destroys personal information unlawfully; fails to report a confidentiality incident; contravenes s. 8.4; fails to take security measures; identifies or attempts to identify a natural person using de-identified or anonymized information; impedes a Commission inquiry; contravenes s. 81.1 (reprisals); refuses to comply with a s. 81.3 demand; or fails to comply with a Commission order, commits an offence and is liable to a fine of $5,000-$100,000 (natural person) or $15,000 to $25,000,000 or 4% of worldwide turnover (others), whichever is greater.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: Individuals are entitled to punitive damages of not less than $1,000 where unlawful infringement of a right under the Act is intentional or results from gross fault.
rule_text_technical: Where the unlawful infringement of a right conferred by the Act or by articles 35-40 of the Civil Code causes injury and the infringement is intentional or results from gross fault, the court shall award punitive damages of not less than $1,000.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must, as a personal information agent, destroy personal information collected more than seven years earlier, except information in files for prevention/detection/repression of offences.
rule_text_technical: Despite section 23, a personal information agent must destroy personal information collected more than seven years earlier; this does not apply to personal information in a file established for inquiry purposes to prevent, detect or repress a crime or statutory offence.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

rule_text: You must, as a personal information agent, establish and apply rules of conduct allowing persons to access and rectify personal information held by the agent.
rule_text_technical: Every personal information agent must establish and apply within his enterprise rules of conduct allowing any person to whom personal information held by the agent relates to access the information according to a procedure that ensures protection and to cause the information to be rectified.

first_instance.law_name: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act) (Quebec, 2021-09-22).

Both require specific authorization from a data protection authority before transferring sensitive personal data abroad, and both include data localization possibilities, but Pakistan's Act also ties this to the PDPA Authority's broader regulatory powers.

Both require a regulatory permit/authorization for cross-border transfers of sensitive personal data, but the Ethiopian rule conditions this on adequacy or safeguards already existing while the UAE rule focuses on certain sensitive data categories and large-volume transfers.

rule_text: You must ensure that anyone working under your authority and any subcontractors comply with the data quality obligations.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

rule_text: You may only collect health-related data from sources other than the data subject when the data subject is incapable of providing the data.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You may only process health data using a unique patient identifier issued by the public authority that is distinct from any other identification number.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You may only associate the unique patient identifier with another identifying number with the express authorisation of the Authority.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

rule_text: The Authority may inspect and assess your security and organisational measures before processing or transfer commences if it considers the processing presents specific privacy risks.
rule_text_technical: Where the Authority is of the opinion that the processing or transfer of data by a data controller entails specific risks to the privacy rights of data subjects, he or she may inspect and assess the security and organisational measures prior to the commencement of the processing or transfer.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

rule_text: The Authority must keep a publicly accessible register of all automatic processing operations of data.
rule_text_technical: The Authority shall keep a register of all automatic processing operations of data, and the register shall be available for inspection by members of the public, in the manner determined by the Authority.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: Whistleblowing rules must preserve fairness, lawfulness, purpose, proportionality, openness, data subject rights of access and correction, and prescribe technical and organisational rules.
rule_text_technical: Rules established under whistleblowing must preserve principles of fairness, lawfulness and purpose; proportionality and accuracy; openness and adequate collection covering scope and purpose, processing of reporting, consequences, exercise of rights of access, correction and deletion, third parties, technical and organisational rules, rights of access not extending to third persons without their written consent, and method of notifying the Authority.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: Authority staff, experts, contractors, or sub-contractors who violate the Act are liable to a fine not exceeding level 7 or imprisonment up to two years, or both.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

rule_text: You cannot intentionally and unlawfully secure access to data, programs, storage media or computer systems without authority; doing so constitutes hacking subject to fines up to level 14 and imprisonment up to ten years in aggravating circumstances.
rule_text_technical: A person who, knowing or suspecting that prior authority is required, intentionally, unlawfully and without such authority secures access to data, programme, computer data storage medium or any part of a computer system, shall be guilty of hacking and liable in aggravating circumstances to a fine not exceeding level 14 or imprisonment up to ten years, and otherwise to level 10 or up to five years.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot unlawfully and intentionally intercept private transmissions of computer data, circumvent protective security, or acquire data within or transmitted to a computer system.
rule_text_technical: Any person who unlawfully and intentionally intercepts by technical or any other means any private transmission of computer data; overcomes or circumvents any protective security measure; and acquires data within or transmitted to a computer system, shall be guilty of unlawful acquisition of data and liable to a fine not exceeding level 14 or imprisonment up to five years.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot unlawfully and intentionally interfere with computer data or a data storage medium by damaging, deleting, altering, obstructing access, or maliciously creating or manipulating data, programs or systems.
rule_text_technical: Any person who unlawfully and intentionally interferes with computer data or a data storage medium by damaging, corrupting, deleting, altering, rendering meaningless, obstructing, denying access, or maliciously creating, altering or manipulating any data, programme or system, shall be guilty of an offence.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot unlawfully and intentionally interfere with the use of a computer or information system, electronic communications system, or critical information infrastructure.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot unlawfully and intentionally disclose computer data, access codes, or commands granting access to programs or data to unauthorised persons, or install destructive programs, or create/alter passwords to access systems.
rule_text_technical: Any person who unlawfully and intentionally communicates, discloses or transmits computer data, programme, access code or command to any person not authorised to access them; activates, installs or downloads destructive programmes; or creates, alters or destroys a password, PIN or code used to access a computer or computer network, shall be guilty of an offence.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot unlawfully acquire, possess, produce, sell, distribute, or use access codes, passwords, or computer programs designed for committing offences, or assemble malicious software for damaging data or systems.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: A magistrate may, on police application, order a person in control of a relevant computer system to produce specified computer data or order a service provider to produce subscriber information for criminal investigations.
rule_text_technical: A magistrate may, on application by a police officer, order that a person in Zimbabwe in control of the relevant computer system produce specified computer data or printout, or that an electronic communications service provider produce information about subscribers, where required for criminal investigation or proceedings.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: If you control computer data subject to a preservation notice, you must preserve specified data for up to seven days (extendable) and disclose specified traffic data to identify service providers or transmission paths.
rule_text_technical: A police officer with a warrant may, by written notice to a person in control of computer data, require preservation of specified data for up to seven days (extendable by magistrate) where there are reasonable grounds to believe data is susceptible to loss, alteration or modification, and require disclosure of relevant traffic data to identify service providers or transmission paths.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As an electronic communications network or access service provider, you are not criminally liable for transmitting information through your system if you did not initiate the transmission, select the receiver, or modify the information.
rule_text_technical: An electronic communications network or access service provider shall not be criminally liable for providing access or transmitting information through its system if such service provider has not initiated the transmission, selected the receiver, or selected or modified the information contained in the transmission, including automatic, intermediate and transient storage solely for transmission purposes.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As a hosting provider, you are not criminally liable for stored information at users' request if you promptly remove or disable access upon a court order or, upon obtaining knowledge of illegal information, promptly inform the appropriate authority.
rule_text_technical: A hosting provider shall not be criminally liable for the information stored at the request of a user if the hosting provider promptly removes or disables access to the information after receiving an order from any court of law to remove specific stored illegal information, or upon obtaining knowledge or awareness of illegal information stored, promptly informs the appropriate authority.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As a hosting provider, if you fail to remove or disable access to information after receiving a removal order, you are liable to a fine up to level 8 or imprisonment up to two years.
rule_text_technical: A hosting provider who fails to remove or disable access to information in terms of subsection (3) shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 8 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years or to both such fine and such imprisonment.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As a caching provider, you are not criminally liable for automatic, intermediate or temporary storage if you do not modify the information, comply with access conditions and update rules, do not interfere with lawful technology, and promptly remove or disable access upon knowledge of removal at source or court order.
rule_text_technical: A caching provider shall not be criminally liable for the automatic, intermediate or temporary storage of information if the caching provider does not modify the information; complies with conditions of access; complies with industry-recognised updating rules; does not interfere with lawful technology to obtain data on use; and acts promptly to remove or disable access upon knowledge of removal at source or court/authority order.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As an internet service provider providing hyperlinks to third-party information, you must promptly remove or disable access upon receiving a removal order or inform the authority upon learning of illegal information, or face fines up to level 8 or two years imprisonment.
rule_text_technical: An internet service provider who enables access to information by providing an electronic hyperlink shall not be criminally liable if they promptly remove or disable access after receiving an order or, upon obtaining knowledge of stored specific illegal information, promptly inform the appropriate authority. Failure to promptly remove or disable access shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 8 or imprisonment up to two years.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: As a service provider, you cannot knowingly enable access to, store, transmit, or hyperlink to information knowing the content is unlawful, or face fines up to level 14 or up to ten years imprisonment.
rule_text_technical: Any service provider who knowingly enables access to, stores, transmits or provides an electronic hyperlink to, any information with knowledge of the unlawfulness of the content of any such information shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine not exceeding level 14 or to imprisonment not exceeding a period of ten years or to both such fine and such imprisonment.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: In criminal proceedings under the Act, electronically generated evidence is admissible, with weight assessed by reference to reliability, integrity, and identification of originator or recipient.
rule_text_technical: In any criminal proceedings for an offence in terms of this Act, evidence generated from a computer system or by means of information and communications technologies or electronic communications systems shall be admissible in court. In assessing admissibility or evidential weight, regard shall be given to the reliability, integrity, identification of originator/recipient, and any other relevant factors.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: A Cyber Security and Monitoring of Interception of Communications Centre is established in the Office of the President as the sole facility through which authorised interceptions are effected.
rule_text_technical: There shall be established a unit in the Office of the President called the Cyber Security and Monitoring of Interception of Communications Centre, which shall be the sole facility through which authorised interceptions are effected, manned by technical experts designated by the agency, and giving technical advice to authorised persons and service providers.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: The Cyber Security and Monitoring Centre must advise government on cybercrime and cyber security policy, coordinate cyber security, operate a whistle-blower system, and oversee enforcement with regard to fundamental human rights.
rule_text_technical: The functions of the Cyber Security and Monitoring Centre shall be to be the sole facility for authorised interceptions; advise Government and implement policy on cybercrime and cyber security; identify intervention areas; coordinate cyber security and establish a 24/7 national contact point; operate a protection-assured whistle-blower system; promote and coordinate activities; provide guidelines; oversee enforcement with due regard to fundamental human rights and freedoms; and provide technical and policy advice to the Minister.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: A Cybersecurity Committee is established as an ad hoc advisory body to the Minister, consisting of eleven members appointed for their expertise in computers, telecommunications, law and policy.
rule_text_technical: There is hereby established a committee to be known as the Cybersecurity Committee which shall be an ad hoc advisory body to the Minister, consisting of eleven members appointed by the Minister for their knowledge in computer and telecommunications, law and policy and skills, including representatives from POTRAZ, ICT ministry, science and technology, justice, ZRP, NPA, defence, CIO, Prisons, the cyber security and monitoring centre, and ad hoc representatives.

first_instance.law_name: Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act, 2021

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Zimbabwe Cybersecurity and Data Protection Act 2021 (Zimbabwe, 2021-12-13).

rule_text: You must ensure the confidentiality of personal data and may not disclose it without prior consent of the data subject.
rule_text_technical: Except by prior consent from the Personal Data Subject as determined by the Regulation, the Controller shall ensure the confidentiality of personal data and shall not disclose it.

first_instance.law_name: Oman Personal Data Protection Law 2022 (Royal Decree No. 6/2022)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Oman PDPL 2022 (Oman, 2022-02-09).

Both prohibit disclosure of personal data to third parties without the data subject's consent except in defined permitted circumstances, though Tanzania's rule cross-references a specific internal section (§ 25) for exceptions.
Both prohibit disclosure of personal user data without consent, independently adopted in different Gulf jurisdictions with similar substantive requirements.

rule_text: You cannot transfer personal data outside Oman if it has been processed in violation of this Law or if the transfer may cause harm to the data subject; cross-border transfers must follow the Regulation's controls.
rule_text_technical: Without prejudice to the competences prescribed to the Cyber Defense Centre, the Controller may transfer personal data and permit transferring it outside the borders of the Sultanate of Oman in accordance with the controls and procedures provided for by the Regulation. The controller is prohibited from transferring personal data if it has been processed in violation of the provisions hereof, or if it is likely to cause harm to the personal data subject.

first_instance.law_name: Oman Personal Data Protection Law 2022 (Royal Decree No. 6/2022)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Oman PDPL 2022 (Oman, 2022-02-09).

rule_text: Individuals have the right to appeal to the Authority against a controller's refusal to refrain from further processing, rectify, complete, erase, grant a request, or review an automated decision; aggrieved parties may further appeal to the Court of Appeal within 30 days.
rule_text_technical: Where a controller has not refrained from further processing under s.14, refused rectification/completion under s.15, erasure under s.16, refused a request under s.17(2), or refused review under s.18(1), the data subject may appeal to the Authority. The Authority shall determine lawfulness, inform the parties, and the controller shall give effect within the period determined; any party aggrieved may appeal to the Court of Appeal within 30 days.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022 (Sri Lanka)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Sri Lanka Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Sri Lanka, 2022-03-19).

rule_text: If you charge fees for the re-use of protected public sector data, those fees must be non-discriminatory, proportionate, and cost-based.
rule_text_technical: Any fees charged by public sector bodies for permitting re-use of protected data shall be non-discriminatory, proportionate and objectively justified, and shall not restrict competition.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: If you operate a data intermediation service, you cannot use the data shared through your service for any purpose other than making it available to data users — including, you cannot use it to train your own AI models or for your own commercial benefit.
rule_text_technical: Data intermediation service providers shall not use the data for which they provide intermediation services for purposes other than putting them at the disposal of data users, and any metadata collected may only be used for the development of the intermediation service.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

Both restrict use of data received through a data-sharing mechanism to the stated purpose, but the DGA rule applies to data intermediation services broadly while this rule specifically prohibits profiling based on Art. 5 Data Act data except where necessary for the requested service.

rule_text: If you provide a data intermediation service, you must structurally separate that service from any other commercial activities you carry out.
rule_text_technical: Data intermediation services shall be provided through a separate legal entity, with the provision of intermediation services being legally separated from any other services provided by the same entity to avoid conflicts of interest.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: If you wish to operate as a Recognised Data Altruism Organisation, you must register on the national public register of recognised data altruism organisations.
rule_text_technical: Entities seeking recognition as data altruism organisations shall register in the public national register of recognised data altruism organisations maintained by the competent authority for the registration of data altruism organisations of the Member State in which they are established.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: To be recognised as a Data Altruism Organisation, you must be a legal entity that pursues objectives of general interest, operate on a not-for-profit basis, and be legally independent from any entity operating on a for-profit basis.
rule_text_technical: An entity registering as a recognised data altruism organisation shall be a legal entity established to meet objectives of general interest as provided for in national law, operate on a not-for-profit basis and be legally independent from any entity that operates on a for-profit basis, and carry out data altruism activities through a structure functionally separate from its other activities.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: If you are a Recognised Data Altruism Organisation, you must maintain a public register of all data altruism activities and publish an annual activity report.
rule_text_technical: Each recognised data altruism organisation shall keep full and accurate records concerning all natural or legal persons that were given the possibility to process data held by that organisation, the date or duration of such processing, the purpose of processing as declared, and any fees paid; and shall draw up and transmit an annual activity report to the competent authority.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: When seeking consent for data altruism, organizations must use a consent form that is machine-readable, sectoral and purpose-specific, and compatible with applicable data protection law requirements.
rule_text_technical: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing and developing a European data altruism consent form, allowing the collection of consent or permission across Member States in a uniform format; the form shall use a modular approach allowing customisation for specific sectors and purposes, be machine-readable, printable on paper and user-friendly, and comply with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: Only entities registered in the public register of Recognised Data Altruism Organisations may use the trust mark 'data altruism organisation recognised in the Union' and the associated common logo.
rule_text_technical: A recognised data altruism organisation entered in the public Union register of recognised data altruism organisations may, in its written and spoken communications, use the label 'data altruism organisation recognised in the Union' as well as a common logo to be developed by the Commission via implementing acts.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

rule_text: Member States must designate competent authorities responsible for the registration of data altruism organisations and for receiving notifications from data intermediation service providers.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities responsible for carrying out the tasks related to the notification procedure for data intermediation services and one or more competent authorities for the registration of recognised data altruism organisations, and shall notify the Commission of their identity.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

Both require Member States to designate competent authorities, but the DSA specifically mandates a Digital Services Coordinator role for supervising and enforcing platform obligations, while the DGA focuses on data altruism and data sharing oversight without this coordinator concept.

rule_text: The European Data Innovation Board (EDIB) is established as the EU advisory and coordination body for data sharing, governance, and cross-border data altruism activities.
rule_text_technical: The Commission shall establish a European Data Innovation Board in the form of an expert group, consisting of representatives of the competent authorities of all Member States, the European Data Protection Board, the EDPS, ENISA, the Commission, the EU SME Envoy, and other representatives, to facilitate consistent practice in data sharing and governance.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Governance Act (DGA) (EU, 2022-05-30).

Both establish EU-level advisory/coordination boards composed of national authority representatives, but the DSA creates the European Board for Digital Services from Digital Services Coordinators for platform oversight, while the DGA creates the European Data Innovation Board for data sharing and governance.

rule_text: You cannot forge personal data for personal benefit or to harm others; doing so may result in imprisonment up to 6 years and/or fines up to Rp 6,000,000,000.
rule_text_technical: Forgery of personal data for personal benefit or to harm others is punishable by imprisonment up to 6 years and/or fines up to Rp 6,000,000,000.

first_instance.law_name: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (UU PDP)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law 2022 (Indonesia, 2022-10-17).

rule_text: The National Data Protection Authority must coordinate with sector regulators including OJK (financial services), Kominfo (telecommunications), and BPJS (social insurance) on data protection matters.
rule_text_technical: The NDPA shall coordinate with sector-specific regulators including OJK, Kominfo, and BPJS, and is empowered to issue sector-specific guidance on automated processing, particularly for financial services, employment, and public administration.

first_instance.law_name: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (UU PDP)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law 2022 (Indonesia, 2022-10-17).

Both rules assign multi-function mandates to a national data protection authority including compliance monitoring, registration, investigation, public education, and cross-border cooperation, but Tanzania's provision is a direct statutory mandate for a newly created Commission while Indonesia's focuses on inter-agency coordination with sector regulators.

rule_text: If you operate an online platform with a recommender system, you must set out in your terms and conditions, in plain and intelligible language, the main parameters used in your recommender system and any options users have to modify or influence them.
rule_text_technical: Providers of online platforms that use recommender systems shall set out in their terms and conditions, in plain and intelligible language, the main parameters used in their recommender systems, including the criteria used to determine relevance, the reasons for those criteria, and whether profiling is involved, as well as any options for recipients to modify or influence those parameters.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must conduct at least annual assessments of systemic risks arising from the design and functioning of your service, including risks from algorithmic systems.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall diligently identify, analyse and assess any systemic risks in the Union stemming from the design or functioning of their service and its related systems, including algorithmic systems, or from the use made of their services, at least once a year and prior to deploying functionalities likely to have a critical impact on identified risks.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

Both require periodic risk assessments of harms arising from online services, but the OSA 2023 focuses specifically on illegal content risks for user-to-user services under UK law, whereas DSA Art. 34 targets systemic risks for VLOPs/VLOSEs under EU law with broader scope including fundamental rights.

Both rules establish a risk-based designation or assessment mechanism tied to volume of data/users and risks to rights, but India's rule focuses on designating Data Fiduciaries as 'Significant' based on data volume, sensitivity, and sovereignty risks rather than requiring periodic systemic risk assessments from large platforms as under the DSA.

rule_text: When assessing systemic risks, you must specifically analyse how your algorithmic systems (including recommender, ranking, and content moderation systems) and targeted advertising contribute to those risks.
rule_text_technical: When conducting risk assessments, providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall take into account, in particular, whether and how the design of their recommender systems and other algorithmic systems, content moderation systems, terms and conditions, advertising systems, and data-related practices influence any of the systemic risks identified.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must put in place reasonable, proportionate, and effective mitigation measures to address systemic risks identified under Art. 34, including by adapting algorithmic systems and content moderation.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures, tailored to the specific systemic risks identified pursuant to Article 34, with particular consideration to the impacts on fundamental rights, including measures such as adaptation of recommender systems, algorithmic systems, content moderation processes, advertising systems and internal supervision.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

Both require platforms to implement systems/processes to address harmful or illegal content, but the DSA applies to VLOPs/VLOSEs with a systemic-risk framing, while the OSA applies broadly to user-to-user services with a duty to minimise illegal content presence.

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must publish the audit report and an implementation report responding to audit recommendations, and transmit reports to the Digital Services Coordinator and the Commission.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines that receive an audit report shall transmit it without undue delay to the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment and the Commission, adopt an audit implementation report setting out the measures taken to implement operational recommendations, and make the audit report and implementation report publicly available, with permitted redactions for confidential information.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must provide vetted researchers, upon reasoned request, with access to data strictly necessary to study systemic risks in the EU.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall, upon reasoned request from the Digital Services Coordinator of establishment, provide access to data to vetted researchers who meet the requirements of Article 40(8), for the sole purpose of conducting research that contributes to the detection, identification and understanding of systemic risks in the Union and to the assessment of the adequacy, efficiency and impacts of risk mitigation measures.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must provide access without undue delay to publicly accessible data on your platform to researchers (including civil society and non-profit organisations) meeting specified conditions.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall give access without undue delay to data, including, where technically possible, to real-time data, provided that the data is publicly accessible in their online interface, to researchers, including those affiliated to not-for-profit bodies, organisations and associations, who comply with the conditions set out in Article 40(8).

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate an online platform displaying advertising, you must ensure recipients can identify in real time that content is an advertisement, on whose behalf it is displayed, who paid for it, and the main parameters used to target them.
rule_text_technical: Providers of online platforms that present advertisements on their online interfaces shall ensure that, for each specific advertisement presented to each individual recipient, recipients can identify in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner and in real time: that the information is an advertisement; the natural or legal person on whose behalf the advertisement is presented and who paid for it; and meaningful information directly and easily accessible about the main parameters used to determine the recipient and, where applicable, how to change those parameters.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: You cannot show advertisements to people based on profiles built from sensitive personal data such as race, religion, health status, sexual orientation, or political beliefs.
rule_text_technical: Providers of online platforms shall not present advertisements to recipients of the service based on profiling as defined in Article 4(4) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 using special categories of personal data referred to in Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: If you operate an online platform, you must provide users with access to a free, effective internal complaint-handling system to challenge content moderation decisions, including those made by automated means, for at least six months.
rule_text_technical: Providers of online platforms shall provide recipients of the service, including individuals or entities that have submitted a notice, for a period of at least six months following the decision, with access to an effective internal complaint-handling system that enables them to lodge complaints electronically and free of charge against decisions taken by the provider on the receipt of a notice or against other specified decisions, and shall ensure that decisions on complaints are taken under the supervision of appropriately qualified staff and not solely on the basis of automated means.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

Both require an internal grievance/complaint mechanism that individuals can access against the responsible entity, but the DSA requires a free, effective internal complaint-handling system for content moderation on online platforms, while India's DPDPA § 13 requires readily available grievance redressal from Data Fiduciaries or Consent Managers with timely response and escalation ability, covering a broader data protection context rather than content moderation specifically.

Both require internal complaint-handling mechanisms for online platforms, but the DSA requires a free, effective internal system specifically for content moderation challenges, while the UK Online Safety Act Section 21 more broadly requires complaints procedures that are easy to access, easy to use, and transparent without the same specificity on content moderation or the free-of-charge requirement.

rule_text: If you operate a VLOP or VLOSE, you must publish enhanced transparency reports every six months, including human resources dedicated to content moderation per official EU language and accuracy indicators of automated tools.
rule_text_technical: Providers of very large online platforms and of very large online search engines shall publish the reports referred to in Article 15 at the latest by two months from the date of application referred to in Article 33(6) and at least every six months thereafter, and shall include information on human resources dedicated to content moderation per official language of Member States, and the qualifications and linguistic expertise of those persons, as well as the indicators of accuracy and related information referred to in Article 15.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).
