Both require transparency reporting on content and safety measures for large platforms, but the UK OSA delegates specifics to OFCOM and applies to its own category of services, while the EU DSA imposes detailed biannual requirements on VLOPs/VLOSEs.

rule_text: The DSA applies to providers of intermediary services offered to recipients of the service that have their place of establishment or are located in the Union, regardless of where the providers themselves are established.
rule_text_technical: This Regulation shall apply to intermediary services offered to recipients of the service that have their place of establishment or are located in the Union, irrespective of where the providers of those intermediary services have their place of establishment.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

Both rules establish territorial/jurisdictional scope for non-EU entities offering services into the EU, but NIS2 Art. 26(3) specifically targets cybersecurity-relevant service categories (DNS providers, cloud, CDN, managed security services, online marketplaces, search engines, social networks) with a registration/representative requirement, whereas DSA Art. 2 applies broadly to intermediary services — same extraterritorial mechanism but different sectoral coverage and obligations.

rule_text: Large online platforms and search engines that reach at least 45 million monthly active users must comply with enhanced regulatory obligations designed to mitigate systemic risks and protect fundamental rights.
rule_text_technical: This Section shall apply to online platforms and online search engines which have a number of average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union equal to or higher than 45 million, and which are designated as very large online platforms or as very large online search engines pursuant to a designation decision of the Commission.

first_instance.law_name: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Digital Services Act (DSA) (EU, 2022-10-19).

rule_text: Your registration is valid for five years and you must apply for renewal within three months before expiry.
rule_text_technical: The period of registration shall be five years from the date of issuance of certificate of registration, and an application for renewal shall be submitted within three months before expiry.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: Public institutions that collect or process personal data are deemed registered upon commencement of the Act and must comply with its provisions.
rule_text_technical: Immediately after commencement of this Act, public institutions which collect and process personal data shall be deemed as registered with the Commission and shall be required to comply with the provisions of this Act.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: When amending personal data, you must not permanently delete the prior version of the document text.
rule_text_technical: The data controller shall, when making an amendment to personal data in a document under this section, ensure that he does not permanently delete the record of the text of the document as it existed prior to the amendment.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You may transfer personal data to a country with adequate data protection laws only where the recipient establishes the necessity for public-interest tasks or lawful controller functions, or where the transfer is necessary and the data subject's interests are not prejudiced.
rule_text_technical: Personal data shall be transferred to country that has a legal framework that provides for adequate data protection if the recipient establishes the personal data is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or pursuant to lawful functions of a data controller, or establishes necessity with no reason to assume the data subject's legitimate interests might be prejudiced.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You must make a provisional evaluation of the necessity for any cross-border transfer of personal data.
rule_text_technical: The data controller shall be required to make a provisional evaluation of the necessity for the transfer of the personal data.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You may transfer personal data to a country lacking adequate protection only if the Commission authorises the transfer based on adequate safeguards through legal, security, and contractual measures.
rule_text_technical: The Commission may authorise a transfer of personal data to a country which does not have adequate level of protection if the data controller satisfies the Commission that there are adequate safeguards with respect to protection of personal data, fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject and the exercise of data subject's rights through adequate legal and security measures and contractual clauses.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: After rectification, blocking, erasure, or destruction of personal data, you must notify third parties to whom the data was previously disclosed.
rule_text_technical: Where the personal data complained of has been rectified, blocked, updated, erased or destroyed, the data controller or data processor shall be required to notify third parties to whom the personal data has been previously disclosed of the rectification, blocking, updating, erasure or destruction.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: As a data processor, you cannot disclose personal data without the prior authority of the data controller.
rule_text_technical: A data processor who, without lawful excuse, discloses personal data processed by the data processor without the prior authority of the data controller commits an offence.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You cannot obtain personal data without prior authority of the controller or processor, or disclose personal data to a third party.
rule_text_technical: A person who obtains personal data without prior authority of the data controller or data processor by whom the personal data is kept, or discloses personal data to a third party, commits an offence.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You cannot offer for sale personal data of another person obtained in breach of this Act.
rule_text_technical: A person who offers for sale personal data of another person obtained in breach of subsection (1) commits an offence.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You must draw up and put in place a code of ethics or policy for personal data protection prescribing ethics and conduct for collecting and processing personal data.
rule_text_technical: Every data controller shall draw and put in place a code of ethics or policy for personal data protection which shall prescribe for ethics and conduct to be complied with during collection or processing of personal data.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: You must submit your code of ethics or policy to the Commission for consideration and approval.
rule_text_technical: Such codes or policies shall be submitted to the Commission for consideration and approval.

first_instance.law_name: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Tanzania, 2022-11-01).

rule_text: Member States must adopt a national policy on managing vulnerabilities, including promoting and facilitating coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
rule_text_technical: As part of the national cybersecurity strategy, Member States shall adopt policies managing vulnerabilities, encompassing the promotion and facilitation of coordinated vulnerability disclosure under Article 12(1).

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for cybersecurity and the supervisory tasks under this Directive.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for cybersecurity and for the supervisory tasks referred to in Chapter VII.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must designate or establish a single point of contact for cybersecurity to ensure cross-border and cross-sectoral cooperation.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall designate or establish a single point of contact; where only one competent authority is designated, that authority shall also serve as the single point of contact.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must designate or establish one or more cyber crisis management authorities responsible for managing large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more competent authorities responsible for the management of large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises (cyber crisis management authorities) with adequate resources and coherence with national crisis management frameworks.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must adopt a national large-scale cybersecurity incident and crisis response plan setting out objectives, responsibilities, procedures, and stakeholder roles.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall adopt a national large-scale cybersecurity incident and crisis response plan laying down objectives of national preparedness, tasks and responsibilities of crisis management authorities, crisis management procedures, preparedness measures including exercises, relevant stakeholders, and procedures for participation in coordinated Union-level management.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must designate or establish one or more CSIRTs responsible for incident handling under a well-defined process covering the sectors listed in Annexes I and II.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall designate or establish one or more CSIRTs that comply with Article 11(1), cover at least the sectors, subsectors and types of entity referred to in Annexes I and II, and are responsible for incident handling in accordance with a well-defined process.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: CSIRTs must ensure high availability, secure premises, redundant systems, trained staff, and confidentiality of operations.
rule_text_technical: CSIRTs shall ensure high availability of communication channels, secure premises and supporting information systems, an appropriate request management system, confidentiality and trustworthiness of operations, adequate staffing and training, and redundant systems with backup working space.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: AI standards bodies shall develop and maintain a vulnerability database that enables voluntary disclosure and registration of publicly known vulnerabilities in AI systems and related ICT products and services.
rule_text_technical: ENISA shall develop and maintain, after consulting the Cooperation Group, a European vulnerability database, including information describing the vulnerability, affected ICT products/services and severity, and patch availability or mitigation guidance, with appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure security and integrity.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational, and organisational measures to manage cybersecurity risks to your network and information systems and to minimise incident impact on service recipients.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage risks to the security of network and information systems used for operations or service provision, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents, taking into account state-of-the-art, relevant standards, cost, exposure, size, and likelihood/severity of incidents.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

Both require managing risks (technical, operational, and broader) associated with AI/digital systems, but Ontario Bill 194 is specific to AI systems in the public sector and adds ethical and legal risk dimensions, whereas NIS2 focuses on cybersecurity risk management for network and information systems across sectors.

rule_text: Your cybersecurity risk-management measures must include at least: risk analysis policies, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, secure development, effectiveness assessment, cyber hygiene and training, cryptography, HR security and access control, and multi-factor authentication where appropriate.
rule_text_technical: Measures shall be based on an all-hazards approach and include at least: (a) policies on risk analysis and information system security; (b) incident handling; (c) business continuity including backup and disaster recovery and crisis management; (d) supply chain security; (e) security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance including vulnerability handling and disclosure; (f) policies and procedures to assess effectiveness of measures; (g) basic cyber hygiene practices and training; (h) cryptography and where appropriate encryption policies; (i) human resources security, access control and asset management; (j) multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication, secured communications and emergency communication systems where appropriate.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

Both require active, specific risk management measures including security against adversarial threats and data quality concerns, but Ontario Bill 194 is AI-specific and adds bias/fairness testing obligations not present in NIS2's general cybersecurity measure requirements.

rule_text: If you find that you do not comply with the required cybersecurity measures, you must take all necessary, appropriate, and proportionate corrective measures without undue delay.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall ensure that an entity that finds it does not comply with the measures provided for in paragraph 2 takes, without undue delay, all necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must communicate to recipients of your services potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies they can take, and where appropriate inform them of the threat itself.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to recipients of their services potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies those recipients are able to take in response, and where appropriate inform those recipients of the threat itself.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: As a DNS provider, TLD registry, domain registration service, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed/security service provider, online marketplace, search engine, or social network, you must submit specified registration information (name, sector, address, contact details, Member States served, IP ranges) to the competent authorities by 17 January 2025.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require entities referred to in paragraph 1 to submit by 17 January 2025: name; relevant sector/subsector/type of entity; address of main establishment and other legal establishments in the Union or representative; up-to-date contact details including email and telephone; Member States where services are provided; and IP ranges.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: As a TLD name registry or domain name registration service, you must collect and maintain accurate and complete domain name registration data with due diligence and in accordance with Union data protection law.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to collect and maintain accurate and complete domain name registration data in a dedicated database with due diligence in accordance with Union data protection law as regards data which are personal data.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Your domain name registration database must contain at least the domain name, registration date, registrant's name, contact email and phone, and the contact details of the point of contact administering the domain.
rule_text_technical: The database of domain name registration data shall contain the necessary information to identify and contact holders of domain names and points of contact administering domain names under TLDs, including the domain name, date of registration, registrant's name, contact email and telephone, and the contact email and telephone of the point of contact if different from the registrant.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: As a TLD name registry or domain registration service, you must implement and publish policies and procedures, including verification procedures, to ensure registration data is accurate and complete.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to have policies and procedures, including verification procedures, in place to ensure databases include accurate and complete information, and require such policies and procedures to be made publicly available.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must make publicly available, without undue delay after registration, domain name registration data which are not personal data.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to make publicly available, without undue delay after the registration of a domain name, the domain name registration data which are not personal data.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must provide access to specific domain name registration data on lawful and duly substantiated requests by legitimate access seekers, replying within 72 hours of receipt, in accordance with Union data protection law.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require TLD name registries and entities providing domain name registration services to provide access to specific domain name registration data upon lawful and duly substantiated requests by legitimate access seekers in accordance with Union data protection law, replying without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of receipt; policies and procedures regarding disclosure shall be made publicly available.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You may voluntarily exchange relevant cybersecurity information with other entities to prevent, detect, respond to or recover from incidents and to enhance overall cybersecurity.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall ensure that entities falling within the scope of this Directive, and where relevant other entities, are able to exchange on a voluntary basis relevant cybersecurity information including cyber threats, near misses, vulnerabilities, TTPs, indicators of compromise, threat-actor information, alerts and recommendations, where such sharing aims to prevent, detect, respond to or recover from incidents or enhance the level of cybersecurity.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must notify the competent authorities of your participation in cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements when entering them and of your withdrawal once it takes effect.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities notify the competent authorities of their participation in the cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements referred to in paragraph 2, upon entering into such arrangements, or of their withdrawal once it takes effect.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Voluntary reporting cannot result in additional obligations being imposed on the notifying entity beyond what would otherwise apply.
rule_text_technical: Without prejudice to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, voluntary reporting shall not result in the imposition of any additional obligations upon the notifying entity to which it would not have been subject had it not submitted the notification.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Competent authorities must have the power to subject essential entities to on-site inspections, off-site supervision, security audits, ad hoc audits, security scans, and requests for information, documents, and evidence.
rule_text_technical: Competent authorities shall have the power to subject essential entities to at least: on-site inspections and off-site supervision including random checks; regular and targeted security audits by an independent body or competent authority; ad hoc audits; security scans based on objective criteria; requests for information to assess risk-management measures; requests to access data, documents and information; and requests for evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

Both rules empower a supervisory authority to order audits of regulated entities, but the Mexican rule is specific to algorithmic audits by accredited third parties with results shared with INAI, whereas NIS2 covers broader on-site and off-site security supervision of essential entities.

rule_text: For important entities, competent authorities must take ex post supervisory action when provided with evidence, indication, or information of alleged non-compliance.
rule_text_technical: When provided with evidence, indication or information that an important entity allegedly does not comply with this Directive, in particular Articles 21 and 23, Member States shall ensure that competent authorities take action through ex post supervisory measures that are effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Member States may require essential and important entities to use ICT products, services, and processes certified under European cybersecurity certification schemes to demonstrate compliance with risk-management requirements.
rule_text_technical: In order to demonstrate compliance with particular requirements of Article 21, Member States may require essential and important entities to use particular ICT products, services and processes certified under European cybersecurity certification schemes adopted pursuant to Article 49 of Regulation (EU) 2019/881, and shall encourage use of qualified trust services.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: You must submit at least your name, address and contact details (including email, IP ranges, telephone), relevant sector/subsector, and Member States served to the competent authorities, and notify any changes within two weeks.
rule_text_technical: Member States shall require entities to submit at least the name; address and up-to-date contact details including email addresses, IP ranges and telephone numbers; relevant sector and subsector where applicable; and list of Member States where services within the scope are provided. Entities shall notify any changes without delay and within two weeks of the date of the change.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Data protection authorities, central government oversight bodies, and national AI standards bodies may conduct coordinated security risk assessments of critical digital services, systems, or supply chains relevant to AI safety and security.
rule_text_technical: The Cooperation Group, in cooperation with the Commission and ENISA, may carry out coordinated security risk assessments of specific critical ICT services, ICT systems or ICT products supply chains, taking into account technical and where relevant non-technical risk factors.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: CSIRTs must monitor and analyse cyber threats and incidents, provide early warnings, respond to incidents, conduct forensic analysis, and on request perform proactive vulnerability scanning of essential and important entities.
rule_text_technical: CSIRTs shall have tasks including: monitoring and analysing cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents at national level; providing early warnings, alerts and information dissemination; responding to incidents and assisting entities; collecting and analysing forensic data; providing proactive scanning upon request to detect vulnerabilities; participating in the CSIRTs network; acting as coordinator for coordinated vulnerability disclosure where applicable; and contributing to deployment of secure information-sharing tools.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Where public awareness is necessary or in the public interest, the CSIRT or competent authority may, after consulting the affected entity, inform the public about a significant incident or require the entity to do so.
rule_text_technical: Where public awareness is necessary to prevent or deal with a significant incident, or where disclosure is otherwise in the public interest, a Member State's CSIRT or competent authority, and where appropriate those of other Member States concerned, may, after consulting the entity concerned, inform the public about the significant incident or require the entity to do so.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: Each Member State must adopt a national cybersecurity strategy setting out strategic objectives, governance, resources, risk assessment, preparedness, and awareness measures.
rule_text_technical: Each Member State shall adopt a national cybersecurity strategy providing for strategic objectives, resources required, and policy and regulatory measures, including objectives and priorities, governance frameworks, mechanisms to identify assets and assess risks, measures for preparedness response and recovery, list of authorities and stakeholders, coordination policies with critical entities frameworks, and a plan to enhance cybersecurity awareness among citizens.

first_instance.law_name: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in NIS2 Directive (European Union, 2022-12-14).

rule_text: If you are a data controller of major importance, you must engage an NDPC-licensed Data Protection Compliance Organization (DPCO) for periodic compliance audits.
rule_text_technical: Registered data controllers of major importance are subject to periodic audits by NDPC-accredited Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs), and must engage a DPCO for annual compliance audits.

first_instance.law_name: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 4 of 2023)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (Nigeria, 2023-06-12).

Both require a designated category of data handler to engage an independent auditor for compliance evaluation, but India's rule applies to 'Significant Data Fiduciaries' under the DPDPA while Nigeria's applies to 'data controllers of major importance' and specifies use of an NDPC-licensed DPCO, making the scope and mechanism meaningfully different.

Both require significant/major data controllers to undergo periodic independent compliance audits by a certified/licensed auditor, but India's rule specifies an annual minimum frequency and uses the term 'Significant Data Fiduciary' rather than 'data controller of major importance', and the auditor certification regime differs.

rule_text: You must apply to the NDPC for authorization for transfers that do not meet the adequacy, safeguards, or derogation requirements.
rule_text_technical: For transfers that do not meet the adequacy, appropriate safeguards, or derogation requirements, controllers must apply to the NDPC for authorisation.

first_instance.law_name: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 4 of 2023)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (Nigeria, 2023-06-12).

rule_text: The NDPC may issue sectoral guidance on automated processing, particularly for financial services, insurance, employment, and public administration.
rule_text_technical: The NDPC may issue sectoral guidance on automated processing, particularly for financial services, insurance, employment, and public administration sectors.

first_instance.law_name: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 4 of 2023)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (Nigeria, 2023-06-12).

Both provisions authorise the data protection authority to issue sector-specific guidance on automated processing with overlapping sectors (financial services, public administration), but are independently drafted under different national frameworks.

rule_text: You must implement appropriate mechanisms for age verification and parental consent.
rule_text_technical: Appropriate mechanisms for age verification and parental consent must be implemented by Data Fiduciaries.

first_instance.law_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in India Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India, 2023-08-11).
Both require implementation of age verification mechanisms for processing children's data, independently drafted with similar substantive requirements.

rule_text: You cannot impersonate another person while providing personal data for any specified purpose.
rule_text_technical: A Data Principal shall not impersonate another person while providing personal data for any specified purpose.

first_instance.law_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in India Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India, 2023-08-11).

rule_text: You cannot suppress material information while providing personal data for any document, unique identifier, proof of identity, or proof of address.
rule_text_technical: A Data Principal shall not suppress any material information while providing personal data for any document, unique identifier, proof of identity, or proof of address.

first_instance.law_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in India Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India, 2023-08-11).

rule_text: You cannot register a false or frivolous grievance or complaint with a Data Fiduciary or the Board.
rule_text_technical: A Data Principal shall not register a false or frivolous grievance or complaint with a Data Fiduciary or the Board.

first_instance.law_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in India Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India, 2023-08-11).

rule_text: You must notify a credit applicant of an adverse action within 30 days of receiving a completed application or within 30 days of taking adverse action on an existing account, even when the decision was made using AI or machine learning models.
rule_text_technical: Under ECOA and Regulation B (12 C.F.R. § 1002.9), a creditor must notify an applicant of an adverse action within 30 days of receiving a completed application (for credit granted on a case-by-case basis) or within 30 days of taking adverse action on an existing account; this requirement applies fully to AI-driven credit decisions.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: If you use SHAP, LIME, or other explainability techniques to generate adverse action reasons, you must validate that the technique accurately captures the actual factors driving the AI model's decisions.
rule_text_technical: Creditors that use SHAP, LIME, or other explainability techniques to generate adverse action reasons should validate that the technique accurately captures the actual factors driving the AI model's decisions, recognizing that not all explainability methods are equally accurate or appropriate for all model types.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: You must base adverse action reasons on local explanations specific to the individual applicant's prediction, not on global feature importance averages across all model predictions.
rule_text_technical: Adverse action reasons must be specific to the individual applicant (local explanations), not global averages across all model predictions; a SHAP value for a specific applicant's prediction reflects that individual's adverse action reasons whereas global feature importance scores do not.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: You must translate technical explainability outputs into plain-language reasons that are meaningful to applicants and that accurately reflect the underlying technical output.
rule_text_technical: Creditors must translate technical explainability outputs (e.g., SHAP values) into plain-language reasons that are meaningful to applicants, and the plain-language reason must accurately reflect the technical output.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: If your AI model cannot generate specific, accurate adverse action reasons using available explainability techniques, you must modify or retrain the model, adopt a more transparent architecture, or supplement it with human review that can produce such reasons.
rule_text_technical: Where a creditor cannot generate specific, accurate adverse action reasons from its AI model using available explainability techniques, the creditor must either: modify or retrain the AI model to support explainability; implement a more transparent model architecture; or supplement the AI model with a human review process that can generate specific, accurate reasons.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: You must comply with the full adverse action notification requirements when AI models are used to make decisions about existing credit accounts, including credit line reductions, account closures, and rate increases.
rule_text_technical: ECOA and Regulation B apply to adverse actions on existing accounts (e.g., credit line reductions, account closures, rate increases), and where an AI model is used to make such decisions, the creditor must comply with the full adverse action notification requirements.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: When an AI-assisted credit decision is based in whole or in part on a consumer report, you must provide FCRA adverse action disclosures including the consumer reporting agency's contact information and the consumer's rights to obtain and dispute the report, in addition to ECOA disclosures.
rule_text_technical: Under FCRA (15 U.S.C. § 1681m), users of consumer reports who take adverse action must provide a notice including the name, address, and telephone number of the consumer reporting agency; a statement that the consumer reporting agency did not make the adverse decision; the consumer's right to obtain a free copy of the consumer report; and the consumer's right to dispute the accuracy or completeness of any information; these requirements apply concurrently with ECOA/Regulation B in AI-assisted credit decisions.

first_instance.law_name: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence

instances.notes: Rule introduced in CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions (CFPB, 2023-09-19).

rule_text: You must obtain new consent if you change the nature, type, or purposes of processing.
rule_text_technical: Consent shall not be considered valid if the nature, type, or purposes of Processing have been changed without obtaining Consent for such changes.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

rule_text: You may process and transfer data without consent for entities supervised by the Central Bank of Jordan, including cross-border transfers as determined by the Central Bank.
rule_text_technical: Processing is lawful without Consent if required for entities under the supervision and oversight of the Jordanian Central Bank to conduct their functions as determined by the Central Bank, including transfer and exchange of Data within and outside the Kingdom.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

rule_text: You may process data without consent for statistical purposes, national security, or public interest.
rule_text_technical: Processing is lawful without Consent if necessary for statistical purposes, national security requirements, or for the public interest.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

rule_text: A Personal Data Protection Council is established, chaired by the Minister of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, with specified members from regulatory bodies, security agencies, the Central Bank, and four sectoral experts.
rule_text_technical: A Personal Data Protection Council is formed, chaired by the Minister, with the Information Commissioner as vice-chair, and including the General Commissioner for Human Rights, President of the National Cyber Security Center, a representative from the Central Bank, two security agency representatives, and four experts representing telecommunications, banking, and information technology sectors.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

rule_text: The Council must approve and monitor implementation of policies, strategies, plans, and programs related to data protection.
rule_text_technical: The Council shall approve policies, strategies, plans, and programs related to Data protection and monitor their implementation.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

rule_text: The Unit may publish a statement of proven violations at the violator's expense through any suitable means.
rule_text_technical: The Unit may publish a statement of the violations proven to have been committed, at the expense of the violator, through any suitable means and methods.

first_instance.law_name: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Jordan PDPL 2023 (Jordan, 2023-09-24).

Both rules authorize the data protection/privacy authority to publicly disclose or publish details of enforcement actions as a deterrent, though the Mexican rule specifically focuses on AI-related violations and public transparency while the Jordanian rule concerns publication of proven violations at the violator's expense.

rule_text: Where a DPIA reveals high residual risk, you must consult the PDPA Authority before proceeding with processing.
rule_text_technical: Where a DPIA reveals high residual risk, the controller must consult the PDPA Authority.

first_instance.law_name: Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Pakistan)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Pakistan Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (Pakistan, 2023-10-25).

Both rules establish tiered/elevated obligations for higher-risk data processing contexts, but Bangladesh's rule uses a regulator-designation model (BDPA designating 'significant data fiduciaries' based on volume, sensitivity, and risk) rather than Pakistan's DPIA-triggered prior consultation requirement, reflecting a different mechanism for identifying and imposing enhanced obligations.

rule_text: You must design and manufacture connected products and design and provide related services so that product data is, by default, easily, securely, and free of charge accessible to users in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, and where technically feasible directly accessible.
rule_text_technical: Connected products shall be designed and manufactured, and related services shall be designed and provided, in such a manner that product data and related service data, including the relevant metadata necessary to interpret and use those data, are, by default, easily, securely, free of charge, in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, and, where relevant and technically feasible, directly accessible to the user.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Before concluding a purchase, rental or leasing contract for a connected product or related service, you must disclose to the user the type and format of data the product can generate, whether data is stored on-device or remotely, retention periods, and methods of access and erasure.
rule_text_technical: Sellers, rentors or lessors of connected products and providers of related services must, before conclusion of the contract, provide the user with information including the type, format and estimated volume of product data the product is capable of generating, whether data is stored on-device or on a remote server, the duration of retention, and the means by which the user may access, retrieve or erase the data.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Gatekeepers designated under the Digital Markets Act cannot be eligible third parties to receive data shared under user requests.
rule_text_technical: An undertaking designated as a gatekeeper, pursuant to Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925, is not an eligible third party under this Article and shall therefore not solicit or commercially incentivise a user in any manner to make data available, nor shall it accept data made available by a user.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party, you cannot use coercive means to access data or use received data to derive competitive insights about the data holder.
rule_text_technical: Third parties shall not coerce, deceive or manipulate the user, nor use the data they receive to derive insights about the economic situation, assets or production methods of the data holder in a manner that could undermine the commercial position of the data holder.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a third party receiving data, you must use it only for the purposes and conditions agreed with the user and in compliance with EU data protection law.
rule_text_technical: The third party shall process the data made available to it pursuant to Article 5 only for the purposes and under the conditions agreed with the user and subject to Union and national law on the protection of personal data, including the rights of the data subject in so far as personal data are concerned.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot share data received from a user with another third party unless the user has contractually authorised it.
rule_text_technical: The third party shall not make the data it receives available to another third party, in raw, aggregated or derived form, unless this is necessary to provide the service requested by the user and the third party has contractually bound that other third party.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You cannot share data received under data access requirements with dominant digital platforms or gatekeepers.
rule_text_technical: The third party shall not make the data it receives available to an undertaking designated as a gatekeeper pursuant to Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1925.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Chapter II obligations do not apply to data generated by microenterprises or small enterprises, except where they act as subcontractors; medium-sized enterprises that recently qualified as such are exempt for one year.
rule_text_technical: The obligations of this Chapter shall not apply to data generated by the use of connected products manufactured or related services provided by an enterprise that qualifies as a micro or small enterprise as defined in Article 2 of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC, provided that enterprise has no partner or linked enterprise that does not qualify as such; medium-sized enterprises are exempt for one year following the date on which they ceased to qualify as small.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where you are obliged under Union law to make data available, you must do so on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory (FRAND) terms in a transparent manner.
rule_text_technical: Where, in business-to-business relations, a data holder is obliged to make data available to a data recipient under Article 5 or under other applicable Union law or national legislation adopted in accordance with Union law, it shall do so under fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms and conditions and in a transparent manner.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Any compensation agreed for making data available must be non-discriminatory and reasonable, taking into account costs of formatting and dissemination and investments in data collection and production.
rule_text_technical: Any compensation agreed between a data holder and a data recipient for making data available in business-to-business relations shall be non-discriminatory and reasonable and may include a margin; in agreeing on any compensation, the data holder and the data recipient shall take into account in particular the costs incurred in making the data available and the investments in the collection and production of the data.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Where the data recipient is an SME or a not-for-profit research organisation, compensation must not exceed the direct costs of making the data available.
rule_text_technical: Where the data recipient is an SME or a not-for-profit research organisation, any compensation agreed shall not exceed the costs directly related to making the data available to the data recipient and which are attributable to the request, excluding any margin.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Users, data holders, and data recipients have the right to access certified, impartial dispute settlement bodies that must adopt decisions within 90 days of receiving a request.
rule_text_technical: Users, data holders, and data recipients shall have access to a dispute settlement body, certified in accordance with this Article, to settle disputes; the body shall be impartial and independent, possess the necessary expertise, and adopt its decisions within a period of 90 days following receipt of a request.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You may apply technical protection measures (including smart contracts and encryption) to prevent unauthorised access, provided they do not discriminate between recipients or hinder users' rights.
rule_text_technical: A data holder may apply appropriate technical protection measures, including smart contracts and encryption, to prevent unauthorised access to data and to ensure compliance with Articles 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9, as well as agreed contractual terms, provided that such measures do not discriminate between data recipients or hinder a user's right to obtain a copy of, retrieve, use or access data.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Third parties and recipients must comply with data holder requests to erase unlawfully used data, cease production of goods derived from such data, and provide compensation for misuse.
rule_text_technical: The third party or data recipient shall, without undue delay, comply with the request of the data holder to erase the data unlawfully used, end production of goods, derivative data or services produced on the basis of knowledge obtained through such data, and provide compensation for misuse.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: A contractual term concerning data access, use, liability or remedies that is unilaterally imposed by one enterprise on another is not binding if it is unfair, meaning it grossly deviates from good commercial practice contrary to good faith and fair dealing.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term, concerning the access to and use of data or the liability and remedies for the breach or termination of data-related obligations, which has been unilaterally imposed by an enterprise on another enterprise shall not be binding on the latter enterprise if it is unfair; a term is unfair if it is of such a nature that its use grossly deviates from good commercial practice in data access and use, contrary to good faith and fair dealing.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Contractual terms that exclude liability for intentional acts or gross negligence, eliminate remedies for non-performance, or grant one party exclusive rights to interpret the contract are conclusively unfair and not binding.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term shall in any case be considered unfair where it has the object or effect of: (a) excluding or limiting the liability of the party that unilaterally imposed the term for intentional acts or gross negligence; (b) excluding the remedies available to the party upon whom the term has been unilaterally imposed in the case of non-performance of contractual obligations; (c) giving the party that unilaterally imposed the term the exclusive right to determine whether the data supplied are in conformity with the contract or to interpret any term of the contract.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Terms that limit remedies, allow detrimental access to sensitive information, prevent use of provided data, restrict termination, enable short termination notice, or permit unilateral price changes without justification are presumptively unfair.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term shall be presumed to be unfair if it has the object or effect of: inappropriately limiting remedies or extending liability; allowing detrimental access to commercially sensitive information; preventing use of data provided or generated; restricting termination rights or preventing data copying; enabling unreasonably short termination notice; or permitting unilateral price changes without adequate justification.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: The party that supplied a contractual term bears the burden of proving that the term was not unilaterally imposed.
rule_text_technical: A contractual term is 'unilaterally imposed' within the meaning of paragraph 1 if it has been supplied by one contracting party and the other contracting party has not been able to influence its content despite an attempt to negotiate it; the contracting party that supplied a contractual term bears the burden of proving that that term has not been unilaterally imposed.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Public sector bodies may request data from data holders only where necessary to respond to a public emergency, where the data cannot be obtained on equivalent timelines and cost by other means, and is genuinely necessary to fulfil a statutory public-interest task.
rule_text_technical: A public sector body, the Commission, the European Central Bank or a Union body may request data from a data holder where there is an exceptional need, namely: (a) the data is necessary to respond to a public emergency; (b) the data holder does not make the data available on request; (c) the data cannot be obtained by other means on equivalent timelines and cost; and (d) the data is genuinely necessary to fulfil a statutory task in the public interest.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Upon a public sector request meeting the conditions of Article 15, you must respond promptly and make the data available, with compensation limited to the direct costs of making the data available.
rule_text_technical: Data holders shall respond promptly to requests for data made by public sector bodies under this Chapter and make the requested data available through appropriate technical means; data holders may be compensated at cost not exceeding the technical and organisational costs incurred to comply with the request, including, where applicable, the costs of anonymisation.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As a data processing service provider, you must remove and not impose commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles preventing customers from terminating contracts, switching to alternative providers, transferring exportable data and digital assets, achieving functional equivalence, and unbundling services.
rule_text_technical: Providers of data processing services shall take the measures provided for in Articles 25, 26, 27, 29 and 30 to enable customers to switch to a data processing service covering the same service type, provided by a different provider, or to on-premises ICT infrastructure, or where relevant to use several providers of data processing services at the same time, by removing pre-commercial, commercial, technical, contractual and organisational obstacles.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Switching contracts must include clauses permitting transitions without undue delay and within a maximum mandatory transitional period of 30 calendar days.
rule_text_technical: The contract shall include a clause specifying that the switching process shall be initiated by the customer and completed within a maximum mandatory transitional period of 30 calendar days following the maximum notice period, during which the service contract remains applicable and the provider shall maintain full continuity.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Switching contracts must include a maximum notice period for switching not exceeding two months.
rule_text_technical: The contract shall include a clause specifying a maximum notice period for the initiation of the switching process, which shall not exceed two months.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Switching contracts must provide a minimum 30-calendar-day data retrieval period after the transitional period, after which all exportable data must be fully erased.
rule_text_technical: The contract shall include clauses providing for a minimum period for data retrieval, of at least 30 calendar days, starting after the termination of the transitional period, and the full erasure of all exportable data and digital assets generated directly by the customer or relating directly to the customer after the expiry of the retrieval period.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: From 12 January 2027, you cannot impose any switching charges on customers of data processing services.
rule_text_technical: From 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services shall not impose any switching charges on the customer for the switching process.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: From 11 January 2024 to 12 January 2027, switching charges may be imposed only up to the direct costs linked to the switching process.
rule_text_technical: From 11 January 2024 until 12 January 2027, providers of data processing services may impose reduced switching charges on the customer for the switching process; reduced switching charges shall not exceed the costs incurred by the provider that are directly linked to the switching process concerned.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: As an operator of a data space, you must publish a description through a single point of contact and implement technical specifications for data quality, portability, security, and governance.
rule_text_technical: Participants in data spaces that offer data or data services to other participants shall comply with essential requirements to facilitate interoperability of data, of data sharing mechanisms and services, including providing a description of the data space through a single point of contact and implementing technical specifications for data quality, portability, security, and governance.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: Smart contracts used for data sharing must be robust against unintended termination, include access controls and lawful processing safeguards, mechanisms to terminate processing and delete data, and logging for traceability.
rule_text_technical: The vendor of a smart contract or, in its absence, the person whose trade, business or profession involves the deployment of smart contracts for others in the context of executing an agreement to make data available, shall ensure that those smart contracts comply with essential requirements: robustness and access control to avoid functional errors and to withstand manipulation by third parties; safe termination and interruption mechanisms; data archiving and continuity; access control on governance and smart contract layers; consistency with the terms of the data sharing agreement; and auditability traceability through logging.

first_instance.law_name: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 on Harmonised Rules on Fair Access to and Use of Data (Data Act)

instances.notes: Rule introduced in EU Data Act (European Union, 2023-12-13).

rule_text: You must comply with this regulation if you are a public or private sector service provider that collects, processes, or stores personal data or user content (in whole or part, permanently or temporarily, using automated or other means) inside or outside Kuwait, where processing relates to advertising/marketing transmission or monitoring data owners' behavior and tendencies.
rule_text_technical: The regulation applies to all public and private sectors service providers who collect, process and store personal data and user related content in whole or in part, either permanently or temporarily using automated means or any other means that are part of a data storage system, whether processed inside or outside the State of Kuwait when it relates to processing activities linked to transmission of advertising or marketing material or monitoring the behavior and tendencies of data owners.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must classify your data for information security purposes following CITRA's data classification policy or global best practices before contracting with a service provider.
rule_text_technical: Any person, whether natural or legal, who wishes to contract with any service provider, shall classify his data for information security purposes by following the data classification policy adopted by CITRA or global best practices.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must provide all service information, conditions, and procedures to change or delete data in easy-to-understand language in both English and Arabic before providing the service.
rule_text_technical: Prior to providing the service to the user, service providers shall provide all information and service conditions as well as request to change or delete data in easy terms in both English and Arabic.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must identify the authorities to which personal data is disclosed.
rule_text_technical: Identify such authorities to which personal data is disclosed.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must provide information on the personal data storage period and storage location, or indicate if storage is unavailable.
rule_text_technical: Provide information on personal data storing period and storage location, or if storing feature is not available.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must inform the data owner if you intend to perform further processing of personal data for purposes other than those for which it was originally collected.
rule_text_technical: Inform the personal data owner in the event that the service provider intends to perform further processing of personal data for purposes other than those for which the personal data was collected.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: If personal information stored by you is incorrectly disclosed or accessed by a third party causing harm to a large number of users, you must notify CITRA, end users, and law enforcement agencies as soon as possible and within no more than 24 hours after reasonably determining the violation.
rule_text_technical: If personal information stored by the licensee is incorrectly disclosed or accessed by a third party, and this disclosure or access causes harm to a large number of users, the licensee shall notify CITRA, end users and law enforcement agencies as soon as possible and in no more than 24 hours after the licensee reasonably determines that there has been a violation of this disclosure or access.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must process and encrypt personal data using mechanisms and standards determined by CITRA according to the level of data specified in CITRA's Data Classification Policy.
rule_text_technical: Measures to ensure the appropriate level of protection for risk response shall include processing and encrypting personal data. CITRA shall determine the mechanism and standards of encryption according to the level of data specified in the Data Classification Policy issued by CITRA.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must establish measures to restore availability and timely access to personal data in the event of force majeure.
rule_text_technical: Measures shall include restoring availability and timely access to personal data in the event of force majeure.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must comply with rules or directives authorized by CITRA on business continuity, disaster recovery, and risk management to ensure persons with access to personal data process it according to your instructions.
rule_text_technical: Comply with any rules or directives authorized by CITRA regarding business continuity, disaster recovery, and risk management to ensure that any regular person with access to personal data processes such data as per the instructions of the service provider.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You must develop internal systems to receive and examine complaints, access requests, and requests for correction or deletion around the clock.
rule_text_technical: Develop internal systems for receiving and examining complaints, requests for access to data, and requests for correction or deletion around the clock.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You are not required to notify the data owner if you have applied appropriate technical and regulatory protection measures to the affected personal data and taken subsequent measures to ensure risks to data owners' rights and freedoms are not escalated.
rule_text_technical: It shall not be necessary to notify the data owner if the service provider has taken the following steps: (a) Appropriate technical and regulatory protection measures were taken, and such measures were applied to personal data affected by the breach; (b) Subsequent measures were taken to ensure that risks associated with the rights and freedoms of data owners are not escalated.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).

rule_text: You are not liable for civil, administrative, or criminal liability for violating content uploaded, processed, or stored by users in your systems unless you become aware of it and fail to take appropriate action.
rule_text_technical: The service provider shall not be held responsible for any civil, administrative or criminal liability if the violating content of the system or user content that violates intellectual property rights of any third party uploaded, processed or stored in the service provider systems, unless the service provider becomes aware of it and fails to take appropriate action.

first_instance.law_name: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024

instances.notes: Rule introduced in Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024 (Kuwait, 2024-02-19).
